bullets: Reading hired Stuart Fenton in August 2025 as head of AI, the first such role at an English football club. Fenton, a lifelong fan, previously worked as an AI consultant and in telecoms, academia and the Department for International Trade. Owner Rob Couhig took control after Dai Yongge's eight years of ownership brought financial chaos, EFL points deductions and relegation to League One, and the club's target is a return to the Championship and then the Premier League.

Speaking at SportsPro AI and Tech at the London Stadium in late September, Fenton said the club's approach is human-centric and data-fuelled, with AI never making decisions. An AI policy protects academy players' data, and ground staff have used AI for grass maintenance formulas at the training centre and the Select Car Leasing Stadium.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Emerging technologies produce recurring effects. Things change quickly in the spaces around them. And innovation comes from unexpected sources. In the spring of last year, Reading Football Club were perched on the brink of oblivion. A disastrous eight-year spell under the ownership of Chinese businessman Dai Yongge had brought ever-worsening financial chaos, multiple English Football League (EFL) points deductions and relegation to the third-tier League One.

That period of neglect reached a terrifying crossroads in April 2025. With Yongge disqualified as an English soccer director, the Royals were warned they had to provide proof of funding or find a new buyer. Failing that, they would be expelled from the EFL. Mercifully, for a club founded in 1871, deliverance came just a few weeks later.

Barrett was physically dominant at Eden Park, while Tupaea is a hard ball carrier who scored two tries in last year's corresponding fixture in Perth.

Harry Potter said New Zealand used Barrett well in the air, helped by Cam Roigard's kicking game. Joseph Suaalii said the Wallabies have adjustments in mind but would not reveal the game plan. Potter came off the bench onto the wing after Len Ikitau left injured, moving Suaalii into midfield. Potter added that tactics around escorting have evolved over the last two years.
Rugby.copy:
The Wallabies are well aware of the threat posed by starting All Black midfielders Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea heading into Sydney’s Bledisloe Test. Barrett was physically dominant at Eden Park on Saturday, with a number of big tackles leading to penalties at the breakdown while Tupaea poses a threat over the ball and hard running in attack.

The pair have established themselves as the All Blacks top midfield combination since former coach moved Quinn Tupaea to 13 last year, which resulted in a breakout performance in Perth in 2025’s corresponding fixture.

Rugby.title: Tana Umaga: 'I think he'll go down as one of the best we've had'
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks captain Umaga played for the 'Canes 122 times through some iconic eras alongside legendary teammates, but never had the pleasure of lifting the trophy at season's end.
bullets: All Blacks defence coach Tana Umaga says Jordie Barrett is on pace to become an All Blacks great and will go down as one of the best the team has had. Barrett made 16 tackles and 13 carries against the Wallabies in Saturday's Bledisloe Cup win, the latest showing in a strong season.

Asked what advice he has given Barrett, Umaga said it was the other way round, adding that he wished he had Barrett's skills and fitness, and praised his competitiveness and consistency. He warned that the Wallabies, at home under Les Kiss, will look for a response in Sydney this weekend and that the All Blacks must be better. Barrett also helped the Hurricanes win the Super Rugby Pacific title in June.
Rugby.copy:
Tana Umaga says Jordie Barrett is on pace to become an All Blacks great, with his latest showing in the black jersey among the best of his 86-Test career. Barrett’s 16-tackle, 13-carry performance against the Wallabies in Saturday’s Bledisloe Cup defence earned plenty of plaudits, the latest in a stellar season for the inside centre, who played a big hand in lifting the Hurricanes to a drought-breaking Super Rugby Pacific title in June.

Former All Blacks captain Umaga played for the ‘Canes 122 times through some iconic eras alongside legendary teammates, but never had the pleasure of lifting the trophy at season’s end. Now defence coach of Barrett and the New Zealand team, Umaga was asked about the advice he’s offered the star midfielder to help him reach new heights in the black jersey.

Rugby.title: Jordie Barrett weighs in on the Wallabies' latest NRL recruits
Rugby.summary: Next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia has lured some of the very top NRL talent across the great code divide, and All Blacks star Jordie Barrett expects the new recruits to be "outstanding" in the 15-man code.
bullets: Jordie Barrett expects the NRL talent moving to rugby union ahead of next year's World Cup in Australia to be "outstanding". Angus Crichton, who helped the Roosters win the NRL title last week, is joining the Waratahs and is reportedly eyeing the No.12 jersey, setting up a Round 4 meeting with Barrett's Hurricanes in Sydney next year.

Mark Nawaqanitawase has signed with Saitama Wild Knights in Japan Rugby League One and has ruled himself out of the Nations Championship. The 11-cap Wallaby is also eligible for Italy and Fiji, and Barrett said he will be back in the Wallabies jersey. Barrett added that Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii is improving every week. The All Blacks are also meeting Kiwi league players, including Moses Leo, before the Rugby League World Cup opener.
Rugby.copy:
Next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia has lured some of the very top NRL talent across the great code divide, and All Blacks star Jordie Barrett expects the new recruits to be “outstanding” in the 15-man code.

Only one of the recent transfers, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, is involved in the Bledisloe Cup series set to conclude in Sydney this weekend, but his former teammate isn’t far behind.

Rugby.title: Two punch-ups, two red cards, no chances left
Rugby.summary: Totoa Auvaa's young career has been derailed by a chaotic 14 months at Saracens which featured violence both on and off the pitch.
bullets: Saracens sacked 21-year-old Samoan Totoa Auvaa on Monday, after announcing an internal investigation into reports that he had been involved in a punch-up in St Albans. A second statement followed four hours later confirming the dismissal. He had joined the club less than 14 months earlier, when it cited his "enormous potential".

Saracens had stood by Auvaa after a nightclub altercation with England cricketers Gus Atkinson and Ben Stokes in June, saying they would not punish him. He was also sent off twice for violent conduct while on loan at Ampthill last season, in November and March, both against Hartpury. Jamie George said technical director Brendan Venter and CEO Ed Coetzee had handled the matter well so the club could focus on the rugby. The club referenced its obligations to supporters, young people and partners.
Rugby.copy:
The end came for Totoa Auvaa via a quick one-two combination. Early on Monday afternoon, Saracens announced an internal investigation into reports that the 21-year-old Samoan had been involved in a punch-up in St Albans.

Four hours later, another statement was released. The investigation was done. Auvaa's fate was decided. A player, flown over and unveiled with a statement mentioning his "enormous potential" less than 14 months before, was sacked.

Rugby.title: Peel relishing Scarlets' Euro reunion with Jones
Rugby.summary: Dwayne Peel is relishing pitting Scarlets against a Newcastle side coached by friend and former half-back partner Stephen Jones in the European Challenge Cup.
bullets: Scarlets head coach Dwayne Peel is looking forward to facing his former Scarlets, Wales and British and Irish Lions half-back partner Stephen Jones, and ex-Ulster boss Dan McFarland, when Newcastle Red Bulls visit Llanelli in the European Challenge Cup on Saturday (20:00 BST). Jones is McFarland's assistant at Newcastle. Peel and Jones are also business partners in a restaurant.

Peel, 45, said the return of Nigel Davies as director of rugby in January has freed him to focus on the rugby. Wales back row Taine Plumtree trained on Tuesday and a final call on his availability will follow. Corey Domachowski and Carwyn Leggatt-Jones are further from selection, while New Zealand lock Tom Allen joins from the Hurricanes this week. Peel said Newcastle have had big investment and will try to keep the ball in hand. Scarlets also face Lyon, Sharks and Castres.
Rugby.copy:
Dwayne Peel is relishing taking on his former Scarlets, Wales and British and Irish Lions half-back partner Stephen Jones, as well as his ex-Ulster boss Dan McFarland, when Newcastle Red Bulls visit Llanelli on Saturday (20:00 BST).

Peel and Jones' relationship off the field has also included being business partners in a restaurant. But the friendships have been put on a brief hold ahead of their European Challenge Cup opener, with Peel saying: "We are in contact weekly, although we haven't spoken this week, weirdly."

Rugby.title: Leicester sign Samoa hooker Asiata
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers complete the signing of Queensland Reds and Samoa hooker Richie Asiata.
bullets: Leicester Tigers have signed Samoan international hooker Richie Asiata. The 30-year-old has played more than 50 times in Super Rugby for Queensland Reds. He is a former Australia Under-20 international who was born in New Zealand and won his first two Samoa caps earlier this year.

Asiata described the move as a new opportunity on the other side of the world. He said he spoke to James O'Connor, Ben Volavola and Izaia Perese about Leicester's history, and that they told him the fans are unreal at home games. He said he is looking forward to getting to know his team-mates, the fans and the culture. He is also in Samoa's squad for next month's Nations Cup games.
Rugby.copy:
Leicester Tigers have signed Samoan international hooker Richie Asiata. The 30-year-old has played more than 50 times in Super Rugby with Queensland Reds. "This is a new opportunity for me on this side of the world," Asiata told the club's website, external.

"I spoke to James O'Connor, Ben Volavola and Izaia Perese, [and] they told me about the history of Leicester. The fans are unreal, it's pretty crazy at home games." "I'm really happy to get involved, I can't wait to get to know the boys, the fans and the culture," he added.

Rugby.title: Wales and Ospreys suffer lengthy Hardy injury blow
Rugby.summary: Ospreys and Wales scrum-half Kieran Hardy faces months out after it was confirmed he needs surgery on an injured knee.
bullets: Wales and Ospreys scrum-half Kieran Hardy faces knee surgery and months on the sidelines. The 30-year-old was helped from the field in the first half of Ospreys' 38-31 win at Dragons on Friday. Ospreys transition coach Richard Kelly confirmed on Tuesday that the injury is serious, and said the exact recovery timeline will not be known until after the operation.

The 32-cap international had been expected to keep his place in Steve Tandy's Wales squad for the November Tests, which begin against Japan in Cardiff on Saturday 7 November. He was Tomos Williams's number two at the 2026 Six Nations and now appears a serious doubt for next year's tournament. The absence may open the way for Ospreys team-mate Reuben Morgan-Williams, and is likely to increase calls for 36-year-old Gareth Davies to reverse his international retirement.
Rugby.copy:
Wales and Ospreys have suffered a significant blow with scrum-half Kieran Hardy facing knee surgery and months on the sidelines. Hardy, 30, started the 38-31 win at Dragons on Friday night, but had to be helped from the field during the first half in evident pain.

He was sent for scans after the game and on Tuesday, Ospreys transition coach Richard Kelly confirmed Hardy needs a spell on the sidelines. "He's had a serious injury and is going to need surgery," said Kelly.

Rugby.title: 'No love lost' Anglo-Welsh derbies still fire Phil Dowson's imagination
Rugby.summary: Sunday's Investec Champions Cup clash vs Cardiff will be the first between the teams in 16 years, since 2010/11, the season in which Saints made it through to the final.
bullets: Northampton Saints boss Phil Dowson believes Cardiff would like nothing more than to travel to the home of the English Champions and claim a Champions Cup win this weekend. Sunday's match is the first between the clubs in 16 years, since 2010/11, when Saints won 23-15 at Franklin's Gardens and 23-19 at the Cardiff City Stadium on the way to the final.

Dowson recalled that meeting as a bad-tempered affair with no love lost, and said English-Welsh rivalry is still very real. Saints have started the defence of their Gallagher PREM title with two wins and a defeat, an identical record to Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship, but have scored 156 points to the Welsh side's 66. Dowson said winning the Champions Cup is difficult given the quality of players from across Europe, but that Saints have proved themselves by reaching knockout games and winning in tough places.
Rugby.copy:
Northampton Saints boss Phil Dowson believes Cardiff would like nothing more this weekend than to travel to the home of the English Champions and claim a shock Champions Cup victory.

Saints have launched the defence of their Gallagher PREM title with two wins and a defeat, an identical record to Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship, but have scored 90 points more: 156 against the Welsh side’s 66.

Rugby.title: Ex-England hooker Singleton joins Glasgow a year after cardiac event
Rugby.summary: Former England hooker Jack Singleton joins Glasgow Warriors on a short-term deal a year after experiencing a cardiac event in training.
bullets: Former England hooker Jack Singleton has joined Glasgow Warriors 13 months after experiencing a cardiac event in training. The 30-year-old has agreed a short-term deal to provide cover during the Nations Championship and Six Nations. He spent six years with Gloucester, scoring 20 tries in 75 appearances, after playing for Worcester and Saracens.

Singleton said the thought of never playing again "definitely crossed my mind" after he had stents and balloons fitted to open his arteries. He described a hereditary condition that was not previously known about and is now more under control through operations and medication. He has done full running sessions since May but is unsure when he will be fit to play. He has four England caps, last played for England in 2022 and is Scottish-qualified through his grandparents.
Rugby.copy:
Former England hooker Jack Singleton has joined Glasgow Warriors 13 months after experiencing a cardiac event in training. The 30-year-old has agreed a short-term deal to provide cover during the Nations Championship and Six Nations.

Singleton spent six years with Gloucester, where he scored 20 tries in 75 appearances, after playing for Worcester and Saracens. He admits the thought of never playing again "definitely crossed my mind" as he had stents and balloons fitted to open up his arteries.

Rugby.title: Dragons suffer Woodman bicep injury blow
Rugby.summary: Dragons flanker Ryan Woodman to have surgery on a bicep injury, ruling him out of contention for Wales' Nations Championship campaign.
bullets: Dragons flanker Ryan Woodman has been ruled out until late December with a bicep injury. The 22-year-old will undergo surgery on Friday after seeing a specialist, and will miss the chance to push for selection in Wales' Nations Championship campaign in November. He started the 19-19 United Rugby Championship draw with Benetton and came off the bench in the 38-26 win over Scarlets.

Woodman is targeting a return for the derbies against Cardiff on 19 and 26 December, before a 2 January trip to Scarlets. Defence coach Dale MacLeod said he is a big loss in a big year as Wales build towards the World Cup, but will not be out for 12 months. Shane Lewis-Hughes has started the last two games at blind-side flanker while new signing Terrell Peita is awaited from New Zealand. Dragons also face injury concerns at prop ahead of their Challenge Cup opener at home to Perpignan on Friday.
Rugby.copy:
Dragons flanker Ryan Woodman has been ruled out until late December after suffering a bicep injury. The 22-year-old will miss the chance to push for selection in Wales' Nations Championship campaign in November.

Blind-side flanker Woodman, who can also play lock, was called up to the Six Nations squad for the injured Taine Plumtree last season. He came on as a replacement in June's uncapped international against the Barbarians at Twickenham but missed out on the Nations Championship summer squad.

Rugby.title: 'Someone do something about it!': LRZ's demand after gruesome injury
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears wing Louis Rees-Zammit has become the latest player to call for artificial pitches to be outlawed after suffering burns to his leg in his side's recent defeat to Saracens in the Gallagher PREM.
bullets: Bristol Bears wing Louis Rees-Zammit has joined calls for artificial pitches to be outlawed after suffering burns to his leg in Bristol's 30-7 Gallagher PREM defeat to Saracens. The 25-year-old Wales international posted an image of his grazed leg on Instagram, asking for someone to do something about the AstroTurf pitches. Similar injuries have been reported on the 3G surfaces at Saracens' StoneX Stadium, Gloucester's Kingsholm and Newcastle Red Bulls' Kingston Park.

Rees-Zammit played home games on Gloucester's artificial surface from 2021 until his move to American football in 2024. World Rugby permitted leggings in 2021, and Jonny May and Newcastle's Christian Wade have worn them. Bristol boss Pat Lam said he rested Pedro Rubiolo, AJ MacGinty and Steven Luatua because of past injuries. Bristol's next game on a 3G pitch is against Gloucester on New Year's Day.
Rugby.copy:
Bristol Bears wing Louis Rees-Zammit has become the latest player to call for artificial pitches to be outlawed after suffering burns to his leg in his side’s recent defeat to Saracens in the Gallagher PREM.

The Wales star is not the first player to suffer such injuries on 3G surfaces used by Saracens at the StoneX Stadium, Gloucester at Kingsholm and Newcastle Red Bulls at Kingston Park.

Rugby.title: Saracens 'delighted' to confirm retention of PWR Player of the Season
Rugby.summary: Premiership Women's Rugby player of the season Olivia Apps has re-signed with Saracens ahead of the 2026/27 seasons.
bullets: Premiership Women's Rugby player of the season Olivia Apps has re-signed with Saracens ahead of the 2026/27 season. The 27-year-old scrum-half and Olympic silver medallist joined from Canada's Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 runners-up side, and helped Saracens end a four-year wait for the English title with a 52-14 win over Trailfinders Women in June's final.

Saracens Women's Director of Rugby Alex Austerberry said Apps had an exceptional first season and has more potential to unlock. The club have signed Ellie Boatman and Beth Wilcock, while Marlie Packer, Rosie Galligan, Laetitia Royer, Beth Blacklock and Deborah Wills have left. Apps is in Canada preparing for back-to-back WXV Global Series fixtures against the Red Roses in Toronto and Ottawa, after Canada drew 26-26 with England at Sandy Park in September.
Rugby.copy:
Premiership Women’s Rugby player of the season Olivia Apps has re-signed with Saracens ahead of the 2026/27 seasons. The 27-year-old Olympic silver medallist was a revelation for the North Londoners last season as they ended their four-year wait to lift an English league title with a 52-14 win over Trailfinders Women in June’s PWR final.

She arrived at Saracens fresh from helping Canada to a runners-up finish at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. Immediately the scrum-half struck up a strong partnership with England playmaker Zoe Harrison and the club charged up the league standings.

Rugby.title: Wallaby Rob Leota exits Bayonne with immediate effect
Rugby.summary: Australia back-row Rob Leota has left Bayonne with immediate effect just over a year after joining, the club have confirmed.
bullets: Australia back-row Rob Leota has left Bayonne with immediate effect, just over a year after joining, the club have confirmed. The 29-year-old was weeks into the second season of a two-year deal and had been sidelined by a knee injury sustained against Montauban in March. Injuries limited the former Rebels and Waratahs forward to 12 appearances for the club.

Bayonne will pay out the remainder of his contract and he is free to join a new club, with a return to Australia a possibility. That could allow him to stake a claim for a Wallabies recall, adding to his 21 caps, and a home World Cup. Bayonne, who sit fifth in the Top 14 after finishing last season 12th, begin their Challenge Cup campaign this weekend against the Cheetahs.
Rugby.copy:
Australia back-row Rob Leota has left Bayonne with immediate effect just over a year after joining, the club have confirmed. The 29-year-old is just weeks into the second season of his two-year deal in France, but the club have let him go after he was sidelined with a knee injury against Montauban in March. This is despite reports that he was due to return to action in the coming weeks.

While the club will pay out the remainder of his contract, he is free to join a new club, with a return to Australia a possibility. Back home, he would potentially be able to stake a claim for a Wallabies recall, add to his 21 caps and feature at a home World Cup.

Rugby.title: Dallaglio's World Cup winner's medal sells for £54K
Rugby.summary: Former England captain Lawrence Dallaglio's 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal is sold for £54,000 at auction.
bullets: Lawrence Dallaglio's 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal has sold for £54,000 at auction at Budd's in Northamptonshire. The former England captain, 54, put items from his career up for sale after being declared bankrupt, including a British and Irish Lions cap that sold for £11,000, an England cap for £8,000 and a 2003 Six Nations Championship winner's medal for £7,500.

The collection had an estimated value of £180,000 and the sales raised £100,500, while a number of items went unsold, including his medals for four Premiership titles with Wasps. Speaking on The High Performance Podcast earlier this month, Dallaglio said he was made bankrupt as a result of getting divorced and had financial problems. He said he sought therapy after the divorce and bankruptcy left him wallowing in "self-pity".
Rugby.copy:
Former England captain Lawrence Dallaglio's 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal has been sold for £54,000 at auction. The 54-year-old put a number of items from his illustrious career up for sale, including medals, trophies and caps, after being declared bankrupt.

A British and Irish Lions cap was sold for £11,000, an England cap for £8,000 and a 2003 Six Nations Championship winner's medal for £7,500. A number of items went unsold, including Dallaglio's medals for his four Premiership title wins with Wasps.

Rugby.title: Louis Rees-Zammit calls for ban on artificial pitches: ‘Someone do something’
Rugby.summary: Rees-Zammit’s legs suffered severe friction burns during Bristol’s defeat to Saracens
bullets: Bristol Bears wing Louis Rees-Zammit has called for an end to artificial pitches after posting images on Instagram of severe friction burns down his right leg following a 30-7 Gallagher Prem defeat at Saracens' StoneX Stadium. The Wales international urged someone to take action over the Astroturf surfaces.

Saracens, Newcastle and Gloucester are the three Prem clubs that play on artificial surfaces. A Professional Rugby Injury Surveillance Project report for 2022/23 recorded match injury incidence of 71 per 1,000 hours on natural grass and hybrid surfaces, against 89 on artificial. Saracens hooker Jamie George said the StoneX pitch meets all rules and that the club trains on artificial surfaces in the week before playing there.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Louis Rees-Zammit has called for an end to artificial pitches in rugby after a graphic Instagram post revealing his injuries after playing against Saracens.

The Bristol Bears wing was part of a 30-7 Gallagher Prem defeat at the StoneX Stadium on Saturday, and used social media to illustrate severe friction burns down his right leg.

Rugby.title: Racing 92 star still in hospital after traffic accident as France prop has 'period of recovery at home'
Rugby.summary: Racing 92 have provided an update on centre Paul Costes following his traffic accident last week, revealing the 23-year-old remains in hospital.
bullets: Racing 92 have said centre Paul Costes remains in hospital following a scooter accident last week that is expected to keep him out for the coming months. The 23-year-old former France U20 international joined from Toulouse over the summer and was last seen in the 48-31 round two home defeat by Lyon.

The club's medical bulletin also said France loosehead Hassane Kolingar is recovering at home after a health issue in round five of the Top 14. The 28-year-old left the field in the first half of the 55-25 win over USA Perpignan on 3 October. Head coach Patrice Collazo said Costes is slowly recovering. Racing travel to Munster at Thomond Park this weekend for round one of the Investec Champions Cup.
Rugby.copy:
Racing 92 have provided an update on centre Paul Costes following his traffic accident last week, revealing the 23-year-old remains in hospital. The former France U20 international was involved in a scooter accident last week that is expected to keep him sidelined for the coming months.

In a medical bulletin shared on social media on Tuesday, Racing revealed that Costes, who moved from Toulouse over the summer, is continuing his recovery in hospital. Elsewhere in the bulletin, Racing revealed that France loosehead Hassane Kolingar is recovering at home after suffering a health issue in round five of the Top 14.

Rugby.title: Borderer Ciaran Beattie oversees comeback for Scotland’s rugby sevens team in Africa after four years away
Rugby.summary: Borderer Ciaran Beattie oversees comeback for Scotland’s rugby sevens team in Africa after four years away The Southern Reporter
bullets: Scotland's rugby sevens team returned after four years in abeyance at Kenya's Safari Sevens in Nairobi, winning one match and losing two before a group-stage exit. They beat a Ugandan select side 17-14 on Friday, then lost 22-0 to eventual winners Kenya Shujaa and 38-17 to SportPesa Forward Legends on Saturday. It was their first tournament since 2022.

Head coach Ciaran Beattie, 49, named a 13-man squad that included five senior sevens debutants and four players with World Sevens Series experience. He said the trip taught the group a great deal and that he was pleased to see Scotland sevens playing again, four years after merging with England and Wales to compete as Great Britain. Kenya Shujaa defended their 2025 title by beating Morans 24-5 in Sunday's final.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland’s rugby sevens team’s comeback after four years in abeyance yielded one victory and two defeats at Kenya’s Safari Sevens at the weekend, leading to a group-stage exit.

Head coach Ciaran Beattie’s squad got off to a winning start in Nairobi last Friday, edging out a Ugandan select side 17-14, but lost twice the day after, by 22-0 to eventual winners Kenya Shujaa and 38-17 to SportPesa Forward Legends, ending their involvement in their first tournament since 2022.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women opt for continuity in squad for two-Test Ireland series
Rugby.summary: Anacadia Minnaar has returned to the Springbok Women squad for October following her late withdrawal from the European tour in September.
bullets: Scrum-half Anacadia Minnaar has returned to the Springbok Women squad for October, following her late withdrawal from the September European tour, replacing Felicia Jacobs. Insaaf Levy is also included because of an injury to Ayanda Malinga. The squad gathers in Stellenbosch this week ahead of a two-Test series against Ireland at Cape Town's Athlone Stadium.

Co-coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have kept the squad largely settled, although Libbie Janse van Rensburg is injured. Captain Babalwa Latsha is named despite leaving the win over Spain with injury. On tour, South Africa lost 50-19 to Wales, beat Italy 41-29 and won 20-nil in Seville. Johannes-Haupt said the group opted for continuity and warned that fifth-ranked Ireland will test them.
Rugby.copy:
Anacadia Minnaar has returned to the Springbok Women squad for October following her late withdrawal from the European tour in September. The scrum-half comes into the squad for Felicia Jacobs, who replaced her in the South Africa squad for WXV Global Series a month ago. In Europe the Springbok Women lost to Wales 50-19, beat Italy 41-29 and picked up a 20-nil victory against Spain in Seville.

Injury to Ayanda Malinga sees Insaaf Levy included in the squad that will gather in Stellenbosch this week ahead of a two-Test series with Ireland at Cape Town’s Athlone Stadium.

Rugby.title: First Games at Talanta Stadium Complex Revealed
Rugby.summary: First Games at Talanta Stadium Complex Revealed Kenyans.co.ke
bullets: World Rugby has confirmed Nairobi's Talanta Sports Stadium as the opening venue of the 2027 HSBC SVNS 2 series, on 23 and 24 January 2027. Montevideo's Estadio Charrua follows on 20 and 21 February, and São Paulo's Nicolau Alayon Stadium hosts the final round on 27 and 28 February.

The announcement follows confirmation of the HSBC SVNS Series and World Championship schedule for 2026/27, as the sevens calendar builds towards the LA28 Olympic Games. The three-tier format links regional qualification to HSBC SVNS 3 and SVNS 2. Construction of the main stadium and most auxiliary works is now more than 94 per cent complete, and the wider complex is also being prepared for the Africa Cup of Nations from 19 June to 17 July 2027.
Rugby.copy:
Talanta Sports Complex is set to host its first series of matches after World Rugby confirmed Nairobi as the opening venue for the 2027 HSBC SVNS 2 tournament. The rugby sevens competition will take place at Talanta Sports Stadium on January 23 and 24, 2027, marking an important sporting event for the new complex.

Nairobi will host the opening leg of the three-event series, followed by Montevideo, Uruguay, on February 20 and 21, before São Paulo, Brazil, hosts the final round on February 27 and 28.

Rugby.title: HSBC SVNS 2: 2027 venues and schedule confirmed by World Rugby
Rugby.summary: World Rugby has confirmed the venues and dates for the three HSBC SVNS 2 tournaments in 2027, with Nairobi, Montevideo and São Paulo set to host the competition.
bullets: World Rugby has confirmed Nairobi, Montevideo and São Paulo as hosts of the three HSBC SVNS 2 tournaments in January and February 2027. The only change is in Nairobi, where the opening leg will be staged at the new 60,000-capacity Talanta Sports Stadium, which is expected to host the opening ceremony and fixtures at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

HSBC SVNS 2 gives six men's and six women's teams a route to the HSBC SVNS World Championship, with the top four in each competition qualifying. Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux will host World Championship events in 2027. The top four men's and women's teams at the end of next year's World Championship will qualify automatically for LA28. General manager Sam Pinder said last season showed the competition's importance as a pathway.
Rugby.copy:
World Rugby has confirmed the venues and dates for the three HSBC SVNS 2 tournaments in 2027, with Nairobi, Montevideo and São Paulo set to host the competition. The three-tournament competition will return to the same cities in January and February, with only one change made to the host venues.

Talanta Sports Stadium will host the opening leg of the season in Nairobi, while the venues in Uruguay and Brazil remain unchanged. Talanta Sports Stadium is a new 60,000-capacity venue in Nairobi, Kenya, and is expected to host the opening ceremony and fixtures at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

Rugby.title: Scottish-qualified Singleton lands immediate URC move after Gloucester exit
Rugby.summary: Former England hooker Jack Singleton will continue his return to professional rugby with Glasgow Warriors after signing a short-term deal with the club.
bullets: Former England hooker Jack Singleton has joined Glasgow Warriors on a short-term deal with immediate effect, just over a year after suffering a cardiovascular event during Gloucester training in September 2025. The 30-year-old, who has four England caps, spent last season in rehabilitation. Gloucester confirmed in August that he was nearing a return to full training but would not be contracted for 2026/27.

Scottish-qualified through his grandparents, Singleton previously made 75 appearances and scored 20 tries for Gloucester, and spent 2023/24 on loan at Toulon. Head coach Franco Smith said he will add top-flight experience behind Scotland internationals Gregor Hiddleston and Seb Stephen. His arrival comes days before Glasgow open their European campaign away to Sale Sharks on Saturday.
Rugby.copy:
Former England hooker Jack Singleton will continue his return to professional rugby with Glasgow Warriors after signing a short-term deal with the club. The 30-year-old has linked up with Franco Smith’s squad with immediate effect, just over a year after suffering a cardiovascular event during Gloucester training in September 2025.

Singleton spent last season undergoing an extensive rehabilitation programme before Gloucester confirmed in August that he was approaching a return to full training, although he would not be contracted at Kingsholm for the 2026/27 campaign.

Rugby.title: End use of artificial pitches - Rees-Zammit
Rugby.summary: Wales and Bristol star Louis Rees-Zammit calls for the end of artificial playing surfaces in top-flight rugby.
bullets: Wales and Bristol player Louis Rees-Zammit has called for an end to artificial playing surfaces in top-flight rugby, after Bristol's 30-7 defeat by Saracens at the StoneX Stadium on Saturday. He posted a photo of a heavily scarred right leg on social media, asking for someone to act on Astroturf pitches. Saracens, Gloucester and Newcastle all play on artificial surfaces in the Prem.

Bristol director of rugby Pat Lam did not select Pedro Rubiolo, AJ MacGinty or Steven Luatua because of the pitch, saying they were coming off big injuries last season. Saracens chief executive Ed Coetzee responded that the surface is under constant review and holds a valid World Rugby Regulation 22 certificate until 1 April 2028, with SF4 documentation submitted to Prem Rugby before the deadline. He said an opposition club's selection is its own business.
Rugby.copy:
Wales and Bristol star Louis Rees-Zammit has called for an end to artificial playing surfaces in top-flight rugby. Rees-Zammit played in the Bears' 30-7 defeat by Saracens on Saturday at the StoneX Stadium, and posted a picture on social media showing a heavily scarred right leg.

Prem clubs Saracens, Gloucester and Newcastle all play on artificial pitches, with the state of the Sarries surface coming under scrutiny this season. Rees-Zammit posted the photo with the caption: "Can we please stop playing on these Astroturf pitches!! Someone do something about it!!"

Rugby.title: Uganda U18 Rugby Sevens Team Wins Gold at Safari 7s Ahead of Dakar Youth Olympics
Rugby.summary: Uganda U18 Rugby Sevens Team Wins Gold at Safari 7s Ahead of Dakar Youth Olympics SoftPower News
bullets: Uganda's Under-18 boys' rugby sevens team won gold at the 2026 Safari 7s Age Grade Rugby Tournament, which was played at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi, Kenya. The Uganda Olympic Committee said the team secured the title on Friday.

The result strengthens the team's preparations for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, the first time the Olympic event will be hosted on African soil. The committee described the victory as a strong statement. It did not give the final score, the opponents in the final or the team's route to the title.
Rugby.copy:
Uganda’s Under-18 boys’ Rugby Sevens team has won gold at the 2026 Safari 7s Age Grade Rugby Tournament, strengthening its preparations for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

The team secured the title on Friday at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi, Kenya, according to the Uganda Olympic Committee (UOC). In a statement congratulating the players and technical team, the UOC described the victory as a strong statement as the team continues preparations for the Youth Olympic Games.

Rugby.title: Alicia Lucas column: Less ‘crunning’ and more sevens for Aussie stars
Rugby.summary: Preseason. The most dreaded word in the sevens world.
bullets: Australia's Maddison Levi and Faith Nathan, in their sixth and ninth preseasons respectively, have swapped part of their usual gruelling preseason for Ultimate Sevens. The competition launched its inaugural season in September 2026, with players spread across six franchises in a multi-round championship. Levi's Pacific Current team were overall women's champions, while Nathan played for Atlantic Novas, coached by New Zealand's Kelly Brazier.

Both players valued the off-field connections made with players from other countries and the chance to play more matches, with less pressure than they are used to. Rugby Australia's director of women's high-performance, Tim Walsh, said the governing body gave the players its full backing to take part, hoping the lessons they learned will pay dividends for Australia's programme.
Rugby.copy:
Preseason. The most dreaded word in the sevens world. Requiring immense physical and mental preparation due to the nature of sevens being fast-paced, high-energy and big physical load, both running and collision-wise. To get yourself ready to compete on the HSBC SVNS Series is something many players dread when that time of year for preseason to begin comes around again. And trust me, it comes. Year after year, season after season, with coaching staff finding new camps, new hills or new gruelling ways to get that extra 1% out of their elite sevens players.

As a former player, I have had it drilled into me from my first ever preseason that it is the scars of preseason that you are meant to remember or draw upon in the depths of a final or the back end of a long hard season. That you’ve been to tougher places repeatedly before than just a single 14-minute game that you are in at that moment.

Rugby.title: The Gallagher Prem may have become the new Super Rugby
Rugby.summary: England's top flight is favouring attack over defence en masse, and its statistics now align, extraordinarily, with the premier southern hemisphere tournament.
bullets: The Gallagher Prem and Super Rugby Pacific have the highest ball-in-play time, the most rucks built and the most tries and points scored, while the Top 14 and URC sit at the opposite, set-piece-focused end. Average penalties awarded in the Prem and Super Rugby Pacific fall below 20 per game.

England head coach Steve Borthwick met Prem directors of rugby in the off-season, with the RFU's refereeing team involved, seeking officiating closer to international demands on the scrum, breakdown and offsides. The contrast showed in the latest round: the Stormers beat the Sharks 39-22, with six of nine tries from close-range mauls, while Bath's 71-48 meeting with Northampton had only three of 18 tries from lineout drives.
Rugby.copy:
Of all the major rugby-playing nations, the professional game has changed more in England than anywhere else since outbreak of Covid-19 in 2020. England lost three Prem clubs because of a shortfall in RFU subsidies during the pandemic. Last year it was revealed club owners were not only plotting radical change, but talking up a post-Covid revolution in the domestic game. The keynotes were conversion of the league into a franchise system, similar to cricket’s Indian Premier League or the NFL in America. That would help centralise commercial operations and distribute revenue equally between the clubs. Financial stakeholders in the game would be buffered from sudden revenue drops with relegation abolished, and promotion would be governed by strict criteria such as the presence of a unique regional footprint, proven financial stability and strong links to the women’s game. An expansion to anywhere between 12 and 14 clubs was envisaged by the start of the 2029-2030 season, with the intriguing possibility two Welsh regions could yet become part of the format.

The radical restructuring of the professional game in England has already been mirrored by a change of culture on the field. The vast majority of teams in the Prem prioritise attack over defence, and that explains the explosion in scoring over the past few seasons, while refereeing has been transformed in the same breath. One of the more extraordinary comparisons in the current season illustrates how the Prem has polarised with Super Rugby at one end of the game, with the URC and Top 14 at the other pole.

Rugby.title: England prop Iyogun signs new Northampton contract
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints loosehead prop Manny Iyogun signs a new contract with the Prem champions.
bullets: Northampton Saints loosehead prop Manny Iyogun has signed a new contract with the Prem champions. The 25-year-old made his England Test debut in July and follows Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock and Tom Pearson in extending his deal at Franklin's Gardens. He has made 104 appearances across eight seasons for the club.

Born in Madrid and raised in Basildon, Iyogun played football before discovering rugby at 14, and joined Southend RFC before being spotted by Saints' academy scouts. He entered the club's pathway in 2016 and made his under-18s debut a year later as a back-row forward, playing two years above his age group. Director of rugby Phil Dowson said he is a fantastic example of what the pathway can produce and has earned every opportunity through hard work, resilience and willingness to develop.
Rugby.copy:
Northampton Saints loosehead prop Manny Iyogun has signed a new contract with the Prem champions. The 25-year-old, who made his England Test debut in July, follows Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock and Tom Pearson in extending his contract at Franklin's Gardens.

A product of Saints' academy, Iyogun has made 104 appearances across eight seasons for the Green, Black and Gold. "It doesn't feel that long ago that I was playing for the under-18s, and now I'm sitting here with more than 100 senior appearances. I've loved every part of the journey," Iyogun told the club's website., external

Rugby.title: Tears, family and 'being boring'
Rugby.summary: After he made a milestone 150th appearance for Ulster on Satruday, Jacob Stockdale tells BBC Sport NI about his tears, family and being "unbelievably boring" about Ireland.
bullets: Ulster wing Jacob Stockdale marked his 150th appearance for the province with two tries against Munster in Belfast, walking out with his daughters Phoebe and Bonnie either side of him. The 30-year-old said it was an emotional day and an amazing experience. His landmark came a week later than planned after he was forced out of the team to face Glasgow in the warm-up.

Ulster came back from 21 points down at half-time to draw with Munster, a week after a 33-33 draw in Glasgow, leaving Richie Murphy's side without a win in their opening three United Rugby Championship matches. They travel to Zebre in the Challenge Cup on Saturday. Stockdale, who missed last season's final defeat by Montpellier with a fractured cheek, said he is focused on Ulster rather than Ireland selection, with the World Cup less than 12 months away.
Rugby.copy:
Jacob Stockdale had run out of the tunnel wearing the Ulster jersey many times before - 149, to be exact. With his daughters, Phoebe and Bonnie, either side of him, he was the first player out on the pitch against Munster as he marked a century-and-a-half of Ulster appearances.

It had been a long time coming for a wing who burst onto the scene in 2016, only for injuries to derail so much early promise. But, after a resurgent few years, he was thankful to reach the milestone with his family by his side.

Rugby.title: Second-half Bledisloe capitulation lays bare Wallabies’ lack of bench depth
Rugby.summary: With two key players unavailable and another suspended, Australia's lack of experienced cover was seriously exposed in Auckland.
bullets: Australia lost the first Bledisloe Test at Eden Park after trailing 17-14 at half-time, with the All Blacks scoring four straight second-half tries and winning the second half 33-5. It was the fourth time this season the Wallabies conceded more points in the second half than the first, and the second of those occasions on which they lost.

Australia's bench had 111 Test caps against New Zealand's 206, with Tom Hooper and Taniela Tupou unavailable and Hunter Paisami suspended. Len Ikitau will miss the return Test in Sydney after failing an HIA, and Jordan Petaia has an ankle injury. Corey Toole has been recalled and uncapped Kadin Pritchard has been called into the squad for the first time.
Rugby.copy:
Another year and another Bledisloe Cup campaign falls at the first hurdle. Australia fans and the Wallabies themselves have seen this movie so many times before, and the proof remains that it’s the hope that really does kill you in the end.

Frustratingly, for the way it ended, it actually started so well. When the Australians scored first at Eden Park and then withstood the inevitable All Blacks fightback to score again before half-time, bringing a 10-point losing margin back to three, the hope was still very much there.

Rugby.title: ‘I’m with you guys’: Shaun Edwards fully focused on Red Roses despite Argentina move
Rugby.summary: England’s Red Roses have praised Shaun Edwards’ commitment to the side despite his impending move to coach Argentina’s men.
bullets: Shaun Edwards will join Argentina's men as defence coach in November, after his consultancy with England's Red Roses ends at the end of October. He will work alongside Mario Ledesma, appointed forwards coach, in Felipe Contepomi's staff. The 59-year-old had previously been linked with a move to Steve Borthwick's England men.

Wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald said Edwards refused to discuss Argentina when she asked him at dinner, telling her he was with the Red Roses. Lock Lilli Ives Campion praised his mindset and energy. England, who beat New Zealand 26-19, face Canada twice, with the Toronto match set to establish a North American attendance record for a standalone women's rugby match, then the USA in New Jersey.
Rugby.copy:
England’s Red Roses have praised Shaun Edwards’ commitment to the side despite his impending move to coach Argentina’s men. Last week, it was confirmed that the experienced coach will join Argentina as their defence coach in November, following the end of his consultancy role with England’s women at the end of October. He will work alongside former Los Pumas head coach Mario Ledesma, who has been appointed forwards coach, in Felipe Contepomi’s staff.

There had previously been speculation that the 59-year-old could join Steve Borthwick’s England men, particularly after it was confirmed that current defence coach Joe El-Abd will leave the international set-up after Rugby World Cup 2027 to become Clermont’s director of rugby in the Top 14.

Rugby.title: Saints tie down fourth England international of the season
Rugby.summary: Newly-capped England international Emmanuel Iyogun has signed a new contract with Northampton Saints, extending his stay at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens beyond the end of the current season.
bullets: Newly capped England loosehead Emmanuel Iyogun has signed a new contract with Northampton Saints, extending his stay beyond the end of the current season. The 25-year-old has made 104 appearances for the club after coming through its academy, and has been part of two Gallagher PREM title-winning campaigns.

Iyogun is the fourth England international to commit to Northampton this season, following Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock and Tom Pearson. He converted from the back row to loosehead after signing his first professional contract in 2019, and won his first cap off the bench in July's 31-24 Nations Championship victory over Argentina. Director of rugby Phil Dowson described his progress as an example of the club's pathway.
Rugby.copy:
Newly-capped England international Emmanuel Iyogun has signed a new contract with Northampton Saints, extending his stay at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens beyond the end of the current season.

The 25-year-old loosehead has already made 104 appearances for Saints after coming through the club’s academy and has been part of two Gallagher PREM title-winning campaigns. Iyogun becomes the fourth England international to commit his future to Northampton this season, following new deals for Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock and Tom Pearson.

Rugby.title: World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup round three review
Rugby.summary: Chile and Belgium will meet in the World Rugby U20 Challenger final after both overcame Brazil and Namibia to qualify for the title-deciding match. Portugal and Romania will battle for the bronze medal, while Canada and Brazil will square off for fifth place. Namibia and Hong Kong China will contest the seventh-place play-off.
bullets: Chile and Belgium will meet in the World Rugby U20 Challenger Cup final, with Belgium beating Namibia 47-22 in the final pool round. Portugal and Romania will contest the bronze medal, Canada and Brazil will play for fifth place, and Namibia and Hong Kong China will meet in the seventh-place play-off.

Romania beat Hong Kong China 29-22 to finish second in Pool A, with wing Matei Bivol scoring a hat-trick. Portugal edged Canada 28-26 to secure second place in Pool B, with winger Rodrigo Socorro scoring his fourth try of the tournament. Canada scored late through Porter Grook and Liam Kinghorn, but the final conversion drifted wide.
Rugby.copy:
Chile and Belgium will meet in the World Rugby U20 Challenger final after both overcame Brazil and Namibia to qualify for the title-deciding match. Portugal and Romania will battle for the bronze medal, while Canada and Brazil will square off for fifth place. Namibia and Hong Kong China will contest the seventh-place play-off.

The final round of the pool stage kicked off with Romania overcoming Hong Kong China 29-22, with the U20 Stejarii finishing second in Pool A. Despite ending on the losing side, Hong Kong China struck first, with fly-half Jack Joyce converting an early penalty to put his team ahead. They added a converted try in the 18th minute as hooker Morgan Hanson eluded the Romanian defence to ground the ball next to the posts.

Rugby.title: Baxter hopes to bring Exeter fans back to Sandy Park
Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says he will do what he can to create a side that can bring crowds back to Sandy Park.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs closed their North Terrace for the first time for a league fixture in Sunday's 34-28 win over Newcastle. Only 7,071 attended the 15,600-capacity Sandy Park, despite the club cutting ticket prices earlier this month. The crowd was lower than the 8,682 present for the opening home league game against Gloucester last month.

Director of rugby Rob Baxter said his job in building the crowd is to make the team perform and win games, and that off-field issues are being looked at by others. Chief executive Tony Rowe said prices for some ticket categories in league, European and cup games up to Christmas have been cut, with the biggest reductions for children and youth tickets. The club was taken over earlier this year by Black Knight Rugby, part of the investment group that owns AFC Bournemouth.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter says he will do what he can to create a side that can bring crowds back to Sandy Park. The club closed their North Terrace for the first time for a league fixture in Sunday's 34-28 win over Newcastle.

A crowd of just 7,071 attended the game at the 15,600-capacity home of last season's beaten Prem finalists, despite the club cutting ticket prices earlier this month. , external

Rugby.title: Fiji appoint Springboks World Cup winner Jake White as new coach
Rugby.summary: White will lead the Pacific Islanders into next year’s World Cup in Australiata
bullets: Fiji have appointed Jake White, who guided South Africa to the 2007 Rugby World Cup in France, as head coach to lead them into next year's tournament in Australia. The 62-year-old replaces interim boss Senirusi Seruvakula after a period of upheaval following Mick Byrne's departure in April. White has been out of work since leaving the Bulls last summer.

White arrives ahead of the Test against Japan in Tokyo on 24 October, which precedes Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy. Fiji lost all three of their games in the competition in July, including 73-8 to England. White said he wants Fiji to play like Fiji with a little more structure, and the best-prepared group ever at a World Cup. Fiji are in Pool C with Argentina, Spain and Canada.
Rugby.copy:

White guided the Springboks to World Cup glory in France in 2007, and replaces interim boss Senirusi Seruvakula following a period of tumult after the departure of Mick Byrne in April.

Rugby.title: India Announces Squad for Asia Rugby Sevens Series 2026 Round 2
Rugby.summary: India Announces Squad for Asia Rugby Sevens Series 2026 Round 2 Sportscape Magazine
bullets: India have named a 12-member senior men's squad for Round 2 of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series 2026, with Mohit Khatri leading the side. The round is scheduled for 17 and 18 October at the Racecourse Ground in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

India finished 12th on their series debut in Round 1 in Suzhou, China, on 29 and 30 August, where they were in Pool B with Japan, the United Arab Emirates and Singapore. Javed Hussein scored the senior men's team's first try in a major series. The men did not qualify for the 2026 Asian Games, where only the women's team will compete in Aichi-Nagoya, and the women finished sixth in the opening round.

India has named a 12-member senior men’s squad for the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series 2026 Round 2, with Mohit Khatri leading the campaign in Colombo, Sri Lanka. Although the men’s team finished at the bottom of the table, Javed Hussein touched a milestone by scoring the senior men’s team’s first-ever try in a major series. Rugby.title: Saracens sack academy player involved in cricket nightclub fracas after another incident
Rugby.summary: 21-year-old Totoa Auvaa has been released by Saracens
bullets: Saracens have released Totoa Auvaa, a 21-year-old member of the senior men's academy, with immediate effect after a further incident over the weekend. The club said his conduct "falls short of the standards expected of everyone who represents Saracens, both on and off the pitch", and that it would make no further comment.

Auvaa was involved in a fracas with members of the England cricket team at a London nightclub in June. He threw a punch at Gus Atkinson but missed and hit an England and Wales Cricket Board security guard, who needed stitches but did not report the matter to police. He avoided formal sanctions from Saracens and the Rugby Football Union at the time, when the club called the incident "regrettable" but said it remained supportive of him.

Totoa Auvaa was involved in an altercation with members of the Test side at a nightclub in London this June, throwing a punch at Gus Atkinson but missing and instead striking an England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) security guard.

Rugby.title: Saracens investigate incident involving academy player
Rugby.summary: Saracens say they have launched an investigation into an incident involving a player from the men's senior academy.
bullets: Saracens have launched an investigation into an incident involving a player from the club's men's senior academy. The incident took place in St Albans on Saturday, and the unnamed player has been stood down from all club duties.
In a statement, the club said it expects the highest standards of conduct from everyone representing it. Saracens will make no further comment until the investigation has concluded.
Rugby.copy:
Saracens have launched an investigation into an incident involving a player from the men's senior academy. The unnamed player has been stood down from all club duties after the incident in St Albans on Saturday.

"Saracens expects the highest standards of conduct from everyone representing the club," a statement said., external "We will make no further comment until the investigation has concluded."

Rugby.title: Seven capped Wallaroos named in Australia NextGen U21 squad
Rugby.summary: Seven capped Wallaroos have been included in the Australia NextGen Under-21 squad that will face New Zealand U21 later this month.
bullets: Seven capped Wallaroos – Waiaria Ellis, Faitala Moleka, Piper Simons, Ava Wereta, Amelia Whitaker, Lily Bone and Ruby Anderson – have been named in the Australia NextGen Under-21 squad. The side will face New Zealand U21 on Saturday 31 October at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch, ahead of the Black Ferns' match against France.

The matchday 23 will be announced on Thursday 29 October, before the teams' inaugural fixture. Head coach Iliseva Batibasaga, a former Wallaroos half-back, said the match creates a pathway that gives young players experience of an international tour and a Test environment. She added that a mix of youth and experience is important, and that she is pleased to be part of the inaugural NextGen U21 coaching group alongside Shannon and Alapeta.
Rugby.copy:
Seven capped Wallaroos have been included in the Australia NextGen Under-21 squad that will face New Zealand U21 later this month. On Saturday 31 October, the Australia U21 squad will face their New Zealand counterparts at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch, ahead of the Black Ferns’ clash with France.

Australia NextGen U21 head coach and former Wallaroos half-back Iliseva Batibasaga has named seven capped internationals in her squad: Waiaria Ellis, Faitala Moleka, Piper Simons, Ava Wereta, Amelia Whitaker, Lily Bone and Ruby Anderson.

Rugby.title: Exeter Chiefs to bolster squad with rising South African lock
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter is set to bolster his squad after agreeing to sign André Goedhals from Currie Cup outfit the Pumas to strengthen his injury-hit second row.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs are set to sign 21-year-old lock André Goedhals from the Pumas in the Currie Cup, with Director of Rugby Rob Baxter looking to ease an injury-hit second row. Italian lock Andrea Zambonin is recovering from shoulder surgery and could still be weeks from returning, while Lewis Pearson is also expected to be out for weeks.

Goedhals was born in Devon and holds a British passport, making him English-qualified. He won Springbok under-20 honours but did not fulfil his early promise at the Stormers before moving to the Pumas. He would be the third Pumas player to join the Gallagher PREM this summer, after JJ Scheepers (Sale Sharks) and Sampie Swiegers (Harlequins). All Black Dallas McLeod is due to arrive from Canterbury at the end of the month.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter is set to bolster his squad after agreeing to sign André Goedhals from Currie Cup outfit the Pumas to strengthen his injury-hit second row. The second row has been a problem area for Baxter, with Italian star Andrea Zambonin on the sidelines after a shoulder operation. Although he is closing in on a return to action, he could still be weeks away, as is Lewis Pearson.

But he is looking to solve his problem by landing Goedhals, who holds a British passport after being born in Devon while his parents lived and worked in England, making him English-qualified.

Rugby.title: ‘A great sense of pride’: Alexandra Chambon named France captain for New Zealand tour
Rugby.summary: With Pauline Bourdon Sansus unavailable for France's three-Test tour of New Zealand, François Ratier has named Alexandra Chambon as captain.
bullets: François Ratier has named scrum-half Alexandra Chambon, 26, as France captain for their three-Test tour of New Zealand. She is the third-choice option after Manae Feleu, who is prioritising medical studies, and Pauline Bourdon Sansus, who is staying in France for personal reasons. Chambon captains FC Grenoble Amazones in AXA Élite 1.

Chambon described "a great sense of pride" in the role and said she wants to support the squad's many new faces. France are without Yllana Brosseau, Siobhan Soqeta and Charlotte Escudero. They opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a 28-14 loss to the Black Ferns in Lyon before beating Australia and Canada, and Chambon said the aim is to beat New Zealand on home soil.
Rugby.copy:
With Pauline Bourdon Sansus unavailable for France’s three-Test tour of New Zealand, François Ratier has named Alexandra Chambon as captain. The 26-year-old scrum-half is the team’s third-choice captain, with Manae Feleu prioritising her medical studies and Bourdon Sansus remaining in France this October for personal reasons.

Captain of her club side, FC Grenoble Amazones, in AXA Élite 1, Chambon will lead an inexperienced France team that will also be without Yllana Brosseau, Siobhan Soqeta and Charlotte Escudero.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly
Rugby.summary: Ugo, Danny and Chris talk tries, Christion Wade, Shaun Edwards and the perfect steak.
Rugby.copy: Can you ever have too many tries? Can a steak be too buttery? Ugo, Danny and Chris tackle all the big topics on this week’s pod after another try-fest at the Gardens. We try to explain why there are so many tries in the Prem and if it is devaluing the product. Ashy’s try record hangs by a thread after Christian Wade’s hat-trick took him to 100 tries. Should there be a draft system for young academy players who aren’t getting enough gametime? We ask Phil Dowson for his thoughts. Shaun Edwards will be coaching at next year’s World Cup, it just won’t be with England.
