Rugby.title: Italy name 30-player squad for WXV Global Series tour of USA
Rugby.summary: Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna has named a 30-player squad to tour the USA for Test matches against the Women's Eagles.
bullets: Italy coach Plinio Sciamanna has named a 30-player squad for two WXV Global Series Tests against the USA Women's Eagles. The first is this weekend in Mansfield, Texas, where Michela Sillari could win her 100th cap if she makes the matchday 23. The second is a week later in Nashville, Tennessee, and Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi captains the squad.

The squad includes Sofia Stefan (108 caps), Beatrice Rigoni (88) and Elisa Giordano (84), plus three uncapped players: Silvia Fent and Mascia Jelic of Benetton Rugby Treviso, and Toulon's Rubina Grassi. Silvia Turani is out of the tour with a knee injury. In September's home fixtures, Italy beat Japan 55-21 and lost 41-29 to South Africa.
Rugby.copy:
Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna has named a 30-player squad to tour the USA for two Test matches against the Women’s Eagles. The squad includes Michela Sillari, who could earn her 100th Italy cap this weekend in Mansfield, Texas, if selected in the matchday 23. Italy will face the Eagles again a week later in Nashville, Tennessee.

Sciamanna has selected a highly experienced squad for the October WXV Global Series fixtures, with Elisa Giordano (84 caps), Beatrice Rigoni (88 caps) and Sofia Stefan (108 caps) among those included.

Rugby.title: Points pile-ups, old-school Saracens and a royal pint
Rugby.summary: After a try-filled round of action, how high can scoreboard inflation climb and what is behind it?
bullets: Northampton beat Bath 71-48 in round three of the Prem, ending Bath's unbeaten start to the season. The 18 tries and 119-point aggregate were the second highest in English top-flight rugby history, behind only Northampton's 94-33 win over Bristol in May. Five of the 10 top-flight games to pass 100 points have come since the start of 2023-24, and the round's five games produced 50 tries, an average of 10 per match.

Northampton head coach Sam Vesty attributed the scoring spike to stricter offside officiating, lower tackle height, game speed and fatigue, and greater attacking intent from teams. Elsewhere, Saracens beat Bristol 30-7 on a defence-led approach under coach Adam Powell, and Bristol rested three players over concerns about the artificial surface. Three of the five games were decided by seven points or fewer, and no side in the league remains unbeaten.
Rugby.copy:
It is worth taking a step back to fully appreciate the scale of scoring in the Prem currently. Ten seasons ago Northampton hosted Bath in round three. As on Saturday, Saints won to end Bath's unbeaten start to the season. The score then was 24-6.

Northampton scored four tries - from Courtney Lawes, George North and David Ribbans (twice). Bath had only two penalties from Rhys Priestland to show for their visit. This weekend it wasn't just a different game. It was like a different sport.

Rugby.title: WRU names businessman Faulkner as new chairman
Rugby.summary: Lyndon Faulkner, the nephew of Wales legend Charlie Faulkner, will take the role at the WRU's annual general meeting on 22 November.
bullets: The Welsh Rugby Union has named Lyndon Faulkner, a 66-year-old former Newport and Pontypool player, as its new chairman. He succeeds Richard Collier-Keywood and will take over at the WRU's annual general meeting on Sunday 22 November. Faulkner has built a business career in the United States, with senior roles at Microsoft and Pelican Products among others.

He takes up the role as the WRU plans to cut the professional tier from four teams to three, with Ospreys and Scarlets competing to avoid being surplus. Cardiff and the privately-backed Dragons have already been confirmed beyond the 2027-28 season. The WRU said his mandate is to lead strategic direction and hold the executive to account, and chief executive Abi Tierney said she and Faulkner are ready to form a formidable team.
Rugby.copy:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has named former Newport and Ponytpool player Lyndon Faulkner as the governing body's new chairman. The 66-year-old is the nephew of legendary Wales and Pontypool prop Tony "Charlie" Faulkner and has become a successful businessman in the United States since his playing days.

Faulkner will take over the role vacated by Richard Collier-Keywood at the WRU's annual general meeting on Sunday, 22 November. He will do so at a time when the WRU is planning to cut the game's professional tier from four to three teams, with west Wales sides Ospreys and Scarlets vying to avoid becoming surplus to requirements.

Rugby.title: Ex-Hurricanes Poua coach takes on key Fiji women’s rugby role
Rugby.summary: Former Hurricanes Poua head coach Fusi Feaunati has been named Head of Women's Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union.
bullets: Fusi Feaunati, the former Hurricanes Poua head coach, has been named Head of Women's Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union. He will connect the pathway from community rugby to the high-performance Fijiana Sevens and Fijiana XVs, working with academy staff, provincial and school coaches and community coaching programmes.

Feaunati was head coach of the Hurricanes Poua in Super Rugby Aupiki in 2025, having previously been an assistant. He was also women and girls lead at the Wellington Rugby Football Union and coached Wellington Pride in the Farah Palmer Cup. The union's General Manager High Performance, Naca Cawanibuka, said the appointment reflects the need to match the growth of women's rugby with stronger systems and support. The article cites 12 teams in the Subrails Marama competition and 16 in the Royal Tea Ranadi tournament.
Rugby.copy:
Former Hurricanes Poua head coach Fusi Feaunati has been named Head of Women’s Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union [FRFU]. The appointment follows growing interest and participation in women’s rugby across Fiji. Currently, 12 teams compete in the Subrails Marama competition, while 16 teams participate in the Royal Tea Ranadi tournament.

Feaunati’s role will focus on connecting the pathway from community rugby to the high-performance programmes of the Fijiana Sevens and Fijiana XVs. Feaunati said: “What excites me most about this opportunity is the ability to help shape a connected women’s rugby pathway across Fiji, from community and youth rugby through to elite international performance.

Rugby.title: Tom Willis steps up to dominate Top 14 in Jack's absence
Rugby.summary: Jack Willis may remain sidelined with a leg injury, but his brother, Tom, has ensured that the Willis family continues to wreak havoc on the Top 14.
bullets: Bordeaux-Bègles flanker Tom Willis made a match-high 18 carries and four turnovers as his side beat Clermont-Auvergne 23-22 at the Stade Marcel Michelin on Saturday. His late breakdown steal in his own 22 secured the win. The 27-year-old, who has eight England caps, came close to a try from a driving maul, but team-mate Maxime Lucu grounded the ball.

A try would have put Willis level with Pau's Rodrigo Marta on six for the Top 14 lead after six rounds. He was named in the team of the week by both Midi Olympique and L'Equipe. His brother Jack, Toulouse's reigning Top 14 Player of the Year, has been out with a thigh injury since round two. Bordeaux begin their bid for a third successive Champions Cup at Gloucester's Kingsholm on Friday 16 October.
Rugby.copy:
Jack Willis may remain sidelined with a leg injury, but his brother, Tom, has ensured that the Willis family continues to wreak havoc on the Top 14. The 27-year-old continued his barnstorming start to his second life at Bordeaux-Begles with a decisive role in his side’s 23-22 victory over ASM Clermont-Auvergne at the Stade Marcel Michelin on Saturday.

Tom made a match-leading 18 carries in the victory, and came close to scoring a try off the back of a driving maul, only for team-mate Maxime Lucu to take hold of the ball in the process of grounding it. Had the try been awarded to Tom, it would have lifted him to joint top of the try-scoring charts in the Top 14, level with Pau’s Rodrigo Marta with six in the opening six rounds.

Rugby.title: 'French Paul doesn't miss... I was just wondering what celebration he was going to pull'
Rugby.summary: The opening month of the 2026 Nations Cup delivered a stream of competitive, high-intensity games, multiple outstanding tries and set-piece battles...
bullets: Hong Kong China beat Uruguay at the World Rugby Nations Cup in July when winger Paul Altier kicked a penalty from about 40 metres, with no time left on the clock, to win the match. Team-mates said his confidence was at its highest after he landed almost every kick against Chile, and hooker Alexander Post, 30, said Altier "doesn't miss".

Former Northampton Saints and Bedford Blues player Matt Worley and Post both returned home after playing in England's Championship, which they regard as underrated. Hong Kong China have qualified for the men's World Cup in Australia, about 11 months away, and have reintroduced a full-time programme for more than 30 players. They face the USA, Canada and Tonga in November, hosting Tonga in their final game.
Rugby.copy:
'French Paul doesn't miss... I was just wondering what celebration he was going to pull' The opening month of the 2026 Nations Cup delivered a stream of competitive, high-intensity games, multiple outstanding tries and set-piece battles, and several great moments and memories that made July a successful start to the newly formed competition.

However, for Hong Kong China, their win over Uruguay tops everything else, as it came down to the final play. With no time left on the clock, the visitors squeezed out a penalty, and there was only one way forward: call for Paul Altier and ask their sharpshooter to send the ball through the posts.

Rugby.title: How the All Blacks left ‘waarheid’ behind at the Garden of Eden
Rugby.summary: The first Bledisloe Cup game between New Zealand and Australia provided further evidence that planet rugby is moving away from South Africa’s sphere of influence.
bullets: New Zealand won the first Bledisloe Cup Test 50-19 at Eden Park, Auckland, on Saturday. They hit their target of more than 100 rucks, lost under one per cent of possession to turnovers and increased ball-in-play time by over three minutes. Penalties fell, and scrum-half Cam Roigard's kicking and the use of double-team chases to contest high balls were singled out for improvement.

Writer Nick Bishop argues that rugby is splitting between South Africa's set-piece-led, physical approach and a faster, higher-scoring style used by most other teams. He notes the 2026 Six Nations produced a record 111 tries. The lineout still averaged about 83 per cent and the scrum was not truly tested, so he cautions against firm conclusions from one match. He suggests South Africa's style may still win another World Cup.
Rugby.copy:
There is the truth of the rugby world, and then there is the truth of South Africa. While the rest of the rugby world is dancing to the compulsive disco-beat under a glitterball of relentless attack, the world champions are waiting for the next World Cup and keeping their counsel; ready to pull the unwary back into the dark alleys outside and brawl with them in the gutter.

The 2026 Six Nations set a new record of 111 tries scored, and Les Bleus hardly noticed that they conceded the most tries [19] and points [130] of any winning campaign in the tournament’s history. The newly-minted Nations Championship in July promptly upped the ante, with an average of one extra converted try scored across the first three rounds.

Rugby.title: What Jason Gilmore says Harlequins 'can’t tolerate' as winless run continues
Rugby.summary: Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore claimed his side restored pride despite a third successive loss of the Gallagher Prem campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford.
bullets: Harlequins lost 28-24 to Sale Sharks at CorpAcq Stadium, their third successive Gallagher Premiership defeat. Sale won through a 73rd-minute penalty try, awarded after hooker Sam Riley was sin-binned for pulling down a maul illegally. Marcus Smith scored two tries on his return from injury and Riley also scored twice, while Sale replied through Elia Canakaivata, Gus Warr and Ben Bamber.

Head coach Jason Gilmore said his side had restored pride after a 48-0 loss to Gloucester the previous weekend and were pleased to earn two bonus points on the road. He said selection would depend on full commitment, adding "we can't tolerate" players being in one week and out the next. Harlequins are 10th with two points from three games. Sale are seventh on nine and play Glasgow next.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore claimed his side restored pride despite a third successive loss of the Gallagher Prem campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford. The Sharks snatched a 28-24 win with a 73rd-minute penalty try after they had been outplayed for long periods by a Quins side smarting from last weekend’s 48-0 humiliation against Gloucester.

“It’s disappointing. We probably created three chances in the first half which we didn’t take which came back to bite us,” said Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore. “Fair play to Sale. They got themselves back into the game with their set-piece but I’m really proud of the boys’ efforts up here.

Rugby.title: Rachel Malcolm challenges Scotland to end losing streak after Australia collapse
Rugby.summary: Scotland captain Rachel Malcolm wants her side to use the energy that will be generated around the quadruple header in Sydney on Saturday to their advantage and go out and put in a performance that they can be proud of.
bullets: Scotland captain Rachel Malcolm wants her side to use the atmosphere of a quadruple-header at Accor Stadium in Sydney on Saturday. Their WXV Global Series match against Australia's Wallaroos opens the day, ahead of two sevens matches and the second Bledisloe Cup Test. Malcolm said the players should enjoy the occasion without being overshadowed by it.

Scotland lost 30-10 to Australia at Hive Stadium on 26 September after leading 10-5 at half-time. Malcolm said the second-half collapse was a fair reflection of the result, and that rain left them with "a mountain to climb". Scotland, ninth in the world rankings, have lost seven Tests in a row, including earlier WXV defeats to Canada and New Zealand. Their campaign ends against the Wallaroos in Canberra on 23 October.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland captain Rachel Malcolm wants her side to use the energy that will be generated around the quadruple header in Sydney on Saturday to their advantage and go out and put in a performance that they can be proud of.

The WXV Global Series clash between the Wallaroos and the Scots will kick things off at the Accor Stadium and will be followed by a men’s sevens match between Australia and Fiji, a women’s sevens match between Australia and New Zealand and then the Wallabies against the All Blacks in the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026.

Rugby.title: Rob Baxter: 'That was bloody stressful and I agree with her'
Rugby.summary: Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter branded his side’s hard-fought victory over Newcastle which earned them a first Gallagher Prem victory of the season “bloody stressful”.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs beat Newcastle Red Bulls 34-28 at Sandy Park on 11 October for their first Gallagher Prem win of the season. Ross Vintcent scored two tries, with others from Sam Harris, Bachuki Tchumbadze and Henry Slade, who kicked three conversions and a penalty. Christian Wade scored a hat-trick for Newcastle, and Max Hicks also crossed.

Director of rugby Rob Baxter called the win "bloody stressful" and said his wife had said the same. He said Exeter lacked defensive energy and were slow to get up off the floor, but improved in the second half, conceding only one score. England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso left midway through the second half with a suspected hamstring overload and will be scanned. Newcastle's Dan McFarland said they made too many second-half errors, and his side play Scarlets away next.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter branded his side’s hard-fought victory over Newcastle which earned them a first Gallagher Prem victory of the season “bloody stressful”. Exeter were careless and error-strewn as the lead changed hands on numerous occasions at Sandy Park before they got their noses in front for the final time to clinch a 34-28 success in front of a disappointing crowd of just over 7,000.

Newcastle overcame an awful start, going behind after only 40 seconds, to make life extremely difficult for the home side, Christian Wade scoring a hat-trick of tries. Max Hicks added another, with Zack Henry converting all four to secure two valuable bonus points.

Rugby.title: Double Bok World Cup winner’s future hangs in balance as ruling looms
Rugby.summary: South Africa hooker Bongi Mbonambi is reportedly awaiting the outcome of a lengthy disciplinary hearing at the Sharks over alleged misconduct during a pre-season team-building camp in August.
bullets: Springboks hooker Bongi Mbonambi, 35, a double World Cup winner with 82 caps, is awaiting the outcome of a lengthy Sharks disciplinary hearing over alleged misconduct at a pre-season camp in August. Rapport reported the incident took place at Bayala Private Safari Lodges before the Sharks' 11 August fixture against the All Blacks. Mbonambi, Trevor Nyakane and Eduan Swart allegedly continued socialising into the following morning.

A ruling is expected within two weeks and reports suggest it could significantly affect his future. His contract runs to 2028 but could be terminated early. He has not played in the opening URC rounds, and coach JP Pietersen said there was "no comment on Bongi". He last played for South Africa against Wales in Cardiff in November. The ruling could affect his chances of a Test return in the November matches against Italy, Ireland and France.
Rugby.copy:
South Africa hooker Bongi Mbonambi is reportedly awaiting the outcome of a lengthy disciplinary hearing at the Sharks over alleged misconduct during a pre-season team-building camp in August.

According to South African outlet Rapport, the 35-year-old was involved in an incident at Bayala Private Safari Lodges before the Sharks’ August 11 fixture against the All Blacks. Head coach JP Pietersen had reportedly allowed players to socialise on a Tuesday evening before returning to full training, but Mbonambi, Trevor Nyakane and Eduan Swart allegedly continued into Wednesday morning.

Rugby.title: Exeter examine extent of Feyi-Waboso injury
Rugby.summary: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury he suffered in Exeter's win over Newcastle.
bullets: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury suffered in Exeter's 34-28 Prem win over Newcastle at Sandy Park, the Chiefs' first win of the season. The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half. He had started all three of Exeter's league games, scoring two tries at Bath the previous week.

Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter said he thinks Feyi-Waboso has overloaded the hamstring, that it is not catastrophic, and that it is more of a concern than a long-term worry. England host Australia, Japan and New Zealand in November in the second half of the Nations Championship. Feyi-Waboso missed this year's Six Nations with a hamstring injury and the second half of 2024-25 with a shoulder injury.
Rugby.copy:
England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury he suffered in Exeter's win over Newcastle. The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half of the 34-28 Prem win at Sandy Park - Exeter's first of the season.

He has started all three of the Chiefs' Prem games this season - scoring two tries at Bath last week. He started all three of England's Nations Championship games over the summer and crossed for tries against Fiji and Argentina.

Rugby.title: ‘I'm inspired’: Why an All Blacks veteran still draws inspiration from his younger brother
Rugby.summary: Speaking to New Zealand-based media from the All Blacks' hotel in Sydney, the 146-Test first-five admitted it was a special night at Eden Park for multiple reasons.
bullets: Beauden Barrett started his first Test of 2026 against the Wallabies at Eden Park, Auckland, alongside his brothers Scott and Jordie. It was the 54th time the three had played together at Test level. Beauden, a 146-Test veteran, said it was a special night and that playing with his brothers meant a lot after missing recent Tests.

Jordie was the All Blacks' man of the match with 16 tackles and 13 carries at No. 12, following strong performances in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series against South Africa. Beauden called him "hands down" the best No. 12 in the world at present and said he is inspired by his work rate and physicality. Scott, who has played 90 Tests, returned from a serious back injury after a non-playing sabbatical for the Crusaders.
Rugby.copy:
Running out alongside your two brothers for the All Blacks would be special enough once, let alone 54 times, but veteran playmaker Beauden Barrett continues to draw inspiration from his younger brothers.

Barrett started his first Test match of the 2026 season against the Wallabies at Eden Park, lacing up the boots alongside two of his younger brothers, Scott and Jordie, for the 54th time at Test level.

Rugby.title: Wade set to break Prem try-scoring record
Rugby.summary: Newcastle boss Dan McFarland is confident Christian Wade will break Prem Rugby's try-scoring record.
bullets: Christian Wade scored a hat-trick in Newcastle's 34-28 loss at Exeter, taking his career Prem try tally to 100. The 35-year-old former England winger needs one more to equal Chris Ashton's record of 101, set in April 2023. Newcastle boss Dan McFarland said he is confident Wade will break the record.

McFarland praised Wade's ability to connect with the squad, his pace and aerial ability, and the professionalism he gained from his time in the NFL. Wade scored most of his tries during seven years at Wasps before joining the Buffalo Bills in 2019, then moved to Racing 92 after his release in April 2022. He returned to England with Gloucester in 2024 and joined Newcastle in 2025. Exeter's Rob Baxter said his side defended Wade well but that Newcastle created good chances for him.
Rugby.copy:
Newcastle boss Dan McFarland is confident Christian Wade will break Prem Rugby's try-scoring record. The 35-year-old former England winger scored a hat-trick in Newcastle's 34-28 loss at Exeter to take his tally to 100 over his career.

Wade needs just one more try to equal Chris Ashton's record of 101, which was set in April 2023. "Christian is a really good man, an excellent connector," McFarland told BBC Sport.

Rugby.title: Exeter edge out Newcastle despite Christian Wade hat-trick
Rugby.summary: Exeter 34-28 Newcastle : A bottom of the table clash fell the way of the Chiefs
bullets: Exeter won their first Prem game of the season, beating Newcastle 34-28 at Sandy Park despite a hat-trick from Newcastle wing Christian Wade. The lead changed hands frequently and the Chiefs only sealed victory in the closing stages. Ross Vintcent scored two tries, with Sam Harris, Henry Slade and Bachuki Tchumbadze adding one each, and Slade kicked three conversions and a penalty.

Max Hicks scored Newcastle's other try, with Zack Henry converting all four to earn two bonus points. Newcastle led 21-19 at half-time, and full-back Jake Dalziel became the club's youngest ever league debutant at 18 years and 54 days. Exeter lost Immanuel Feyi-Waboso to a leg problem, and Newcastle prop Adam Brocklebank was sin-binned late on.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. A hat-trick from Newcastle wing Christian Wade was not enough to stop Exeter claiming their first Gallagher Prem win of the season as they edged a topsy-turvy game at Sandy Park 34-28.

The lead frequently changed hands and it was not until the dying stages that the Chiefs were able to seal victory. Max Hicks scored Newcastle’s other try, with Zack Henry converting all four to secure two valuable bonus points.

Rugby.title: Sale complete late win to leave Harlequins bottom of table
Rugby.summary: Sale 28-24 Harlequins: Marcus Smith’s tries threaten a schok result but Sale came back to win
bullets: Sale beat Harlequins 28-24 at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford, sealing victory with a 73rd-minute penalty try, to leave Quins bottom of the Prem after a third successive defeat. Marcus Smith, returning from a finger injury, scored two tries in the opening quarter, and Quins led 17-14 at half-time having had two tries disallowed.

Sale, who had lost on the opening day to Bristol, have now beaten Saracens and Harlequins in successive weeks, and it was their fifth straight win against Quins in the league and Europe. Jason Gilmore's side made seven changes after a 48-0 defeat by Gloucester, their worst league loss in 26 years. Hooker Sam Riley, who scored two tries, was sin-binned for the infringement that led to the penalty try.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Harlequins’ troubled start to the Gallagher Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford.

The Sharks left it late but came from behind to snatch a 28-24 success with a 73rd-minute penalty try, after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to threaten a shock win for the visitors.

Rugby.title: Late Sale penalty try continues Harlequins woes
Rugby.summary: Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continues with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium.
bullets: Harlequins lost a third successive Prem game, going down to Sale at CorpAcq Stadium after a 73rd-minute penalty try. Marcus Smith, back from a finger injury, scored two tries in the opening quarter, and Quins led 17-14 at half-time, with two further tries ruled out by the television match official. The result leaves Quins bottom of the table.

Sale, who also beat Saracens last week, scored through Elia Canakaivata, Gus Warr and Ben Bamber, and won with a rumbling maul that drove Quins back 30 metres. Referee Christophe Ridley awarded the penalty try and sent hooker Sam Riley to the sin-bin. Harlequins, beaten 48-0 by Gloucester the previous weekend, now face Vannes at home in the Challenge Cup next week.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium. The Sharks came from behind to win the game with a 73rd-minute penalty try after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to give Quins an early lead.

After their opening-day reverse to Bristol at home, Sale have bounced back strongly with back-to-back wins over Saracens and Quins. Despite their first points of the season, the loss leaves Quins rooted to the foot of the table.

Rugby.title: Wade scores 100th Prem try as Newcastle lose to Exeter
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade becomes just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 loss at Exeter.
bullets: Christian Wade became the second player to score 100 Premiership Rugby tries, claiming a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter. The 35-year-old scored twice in the first half, the second giving Newcastle a two-point half-time lead, and added a third early in the second half after a Henry Slade error. He is now one short of the all-time record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023.

Exeter secured a bonus-point first win of the season through tries from Ross Vintcent, who scored after 38 seconds on his return from injury, Sam Harris and Bachuki Tchumbadze, plus a 64th-minute Slade penalty. The result keeps Exeter eighth, four points behind leaders Gloucester, while winless Newcastle are second-from-bottom. A crowd of 7,071 meant Sandy Park's North Terrace was closed for the first time for a Prem game.
Rugby.copy:
Christian Wade became just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter. Wade, 35, went over twice in the first half - his second giving the Red Bulls a two-point half-time lead - before pouncing on a Henry Slade error to race in for a third early in the second half.

Newcastle's former England winger is now just one try off the all-time Prem try record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023. Wade, who spent four years trying to break into the NFL from 2018, returned to the Prem in 2024 with Gloucester after two years at French side Racing 92, last year moving to Newcastle after a brief spell at rugby league's Wigan Warriors.

Rugby.title: Davies urged to reverse retirement for World Cup
Rugby.summary: Ex-Wales hooker Scott Baldwin is convinced the 36-year-old's World Cup know-how can still help Wales in Australia.
bullets: Former Wales hooker Scott Baldwin has urged scrum-half Gareth Davies to reverse his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup. Davies, 36, retired from Test rugby in 2024 but came off the bench to spark a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down against Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday, securing the club's first win of the season.

Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport that Davies could be valuable in a World Cup quarter-final against England, questioning Wales' depth behind Tomos Williams. Davies won 77 caps and toured twice with the British and Irish Lions, and will be 37 at the tournament, where Wales face Zimbabwe, Tonga and England in Pool F. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies praised his contribution as "superb".
Rugby.copy:
Gareth Davies has been urged to rethink his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup by former Wales team-mate Scott Baldwin. The 36-year-old scrum-half sparked a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down to beat Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday.

Davies retired from Test rugby in 2024 but ex-Wales hooker Baldwin believes the veteran could still thrive at a fourth World Cup next year. "He could be just what you want in a quarter-final of a World Cup, in a Wales-England fixture in 12 months' time," Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport.

Rugby.title: Fight for Wales spots heats up as under-threat regions win
Rugby.summary: The talking points from round three of URC as Ospreys and Scarlets get first win and players try to impress Wales boss Steve Tandy.
Rugby.copy:
There was western relief after Ospreys and Scarlets got up and running in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) season. The two sides are playing amid uncertainty over their futures under controversial Welsh Rugby Union plans, yet produced the goods on the pitch in round three.

Ospreys won an engrossing derby against Dragons at Rodney Parade, inflicting a first defeat of the season on their hosts, while Scarlets sneaked past Benetton thanks to Sam Costelow's late penalty.

Rugby.title: Ulster playing games like training sessions
Rugby.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach Richie Murphy says Ulster are "playing matches like they're training sessions" as he expressed his disappointment with his side's slow start in Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.

Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.

Rugby.title: Leinster stroll past Cardiff for happy homecoming
Rugby.summary: Champions Leinster score five tries to beat Cardiff in Dublin for their first win of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship campaign.
Rugby.copy:
Champions Leinster made a successful return to the revamped Laya Arena by beating Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship (URC). The Irish province recorded their first victory of the 2026-27 season in front of 20,600 supporters, and condemned the Blue and Blacks to a first loss.

Leinster scored three tries inside the first quarter through Hugo Keenan, Jimmy O'Brien and Jack Conan, then O'Brien's second in the 37th minute secured the four-try bonus. But, with a raft of Ireland internationals making their first outings of the campaign, the second half was flat and scoreless until Jamie Osborne went over with five minutes to go.

Rugby.title: Caluori scores as Saracens too strong for Bristol
Rugby.summary: Noah Caluori gets on the scoresheet as Saracens continue their hold over Bristol Bears at the StoneX Stadium with a 30-7 victory.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: Caluori, O'Driscoll, penalty, J. Bracken Cons: Farrell Pens: Farrell 2 Saracens continued their hold over Bristol Bears at the StoneX Stadium with a convincing 30-7 victory.

Bristol have now failed to win in all eight of their Prem visits to Saracens' home since they reached the top flight, with this loss also their first defeat of the 2026-27 campaign.

Rugby.title: Edinburgh top URC after bonus-point win over Zebre
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh go top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre makes it three wins from three.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: M. Currie, Douglas, Bradbury, T. Currie Cons: Grayson 3 Pens: Grayson Edinburgh went top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre made it three wins from three for Sean Everitt's injury-hit side.

James Grayson kicked a penalty to put the visitors in front early on, but after winger Malelili Satala was sin-binned for a deliberate knock-on, Italy scrum-half Alessandro Fusco put Zebre in front with the game's first try.

Racket.title: Daniil Medvedev makes U-turn after thinking ‘what is Novak Djokovic talking about?’ at Shanghai Masters
Racket.summary: Medvedev has changed his mind about Djokovic's Shanghai court speed comments. The post Daniil Medvedev makes U-turn after thinking ‘what is Novak Djokovic talking about?’ at Shanghai Masters appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Daniil Medvedev beat Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4 7-5 in the Shanghai Masters fourth round on Stadium Court, taking his head-to-head record against the Greek to 11-5. The world number five said he served well and had no break points to save.

Medvedev said he had been baffled by Novak Djokovic's claim that the Stadium Court was "super quick" and completely different to Beijing, because the Grandstand 2 court he played earlier felt the same or slower. In the warm-up on Stadium Court he realised it was very fast and had to reset, then played aggressively. The 2019 champion called Shanghai one of his favourite stops on tour.
Racket.copy:
Daniil Medvedev gave his verdict on a claim Novak Djokovic made about the Shanghai Masters court speed after his victory over Stefanos Tsitsipas. The world No 5 delivered a stellar display to prevail 6-4, 7-5 against 43rd-ranked Tsitsipas in the fourth round at the Masters 1000 tournament on Wednesday.

Former world No 1 Medvedev now holds a 11-5 record against his long-time rival Tsitsipas — who is a former world No 3. Medvedev’s match with the Greek was played on Stadium Court — the main show court at the Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena in Shanghai.

Racket.title: BWF World Junior Championships 2026: India Records Wins Across Singles And Doubles In Cairo

bullets: India won most of its matches on the day at the BWF World Junior Championships 2026 in Cairo, losing only two across singles, doubles and mixed events. Racket.title: Finding Renée Richards: the complicated past and present of a trans sports pioneer
Racket.summary: In 1977, Richards sued to play in the US Open after transitioning. Now she supports bans on trans athletes in women’s sports. A new biography explores a complex legacy It was a story that dominated tennis headlines back in 1977: Dr Renée Richards, an ophthalmologist who excelled as a male amateur player before a sex-change operation, was suing for the right to play in the women’s draw of the US Open. Where did Richards go for legal assistance? None other than Roy Cohn. Better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump, Cohn turned his attention to fighting for Richards’s inclusion. His firm successfully argued the case – part of the narrative of a new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman. Continue reading...
bullets: A new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis's Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman, revisits the 1977 lawsuit in which Richards, an ophthalmologist who had played as a male amateur before a sex-change operation, sued for the right to play in the women's US Open draw. Roy Cohn's firm successfully argued the case, though the decision was limited to Richards and set no precedent for other trans people.

Kliegman, a trans and non-binary sports journalist, drew on Richards' autobiographies, interview transcripts from an unpublished memoir and several in-person interviews with Richards, now 92. Kliegman said Richards now believes trans women and girls should not play women's sports unless they have not undergone male puberty, a reversal of her 1977 position that created tension between them. At Richards' wish, the book uses her former name and he/him pronouns for her early life.
Racket.copy:
It was a story that dominated tennis headlines back in 1977: Dr Renée Richards, an ophthalmologist who excelled as a male amateur player before a sex-change operation, was suing for the right to play in the women’s draw of the US Open. Where did Richards go for legal assistance? None other than Roy Cohn.

Better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump, Cohn turned his attention to fighting for Richards’s inclusion. His firm successfully argued the case – part of the narrative of a new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman.

Racket.summary: Speculation is rife on social media. The post ITIA issue official response to claims Gael Monfils has quietly retired early appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Gael Monfils is now officially retired, with his status changed on the International Tennis Integrity Agency website and confirmed by its head of communication to L'Equipe. He is no longer authorised to take part in tournaments. He had said he would retire at the end of 2026 and was expected to finish at the Paris Masters, from 2 to 8 November, which would have been his 12th appearance there.

The ITIA said he would need six months of out-of-competition testing to return, as Serena Williams did. Monfils won 13 ATP Tour titles, including three at ATP 500 level, and reached three Masters finals: Paris in 2009 and 2010, losing to Novak Djokovic and Robin Soderling, and Monte Carlo in 2016, losing to Rafael Nadal. He also reached the semi-finals of Roland Garros and the US Open.
Racket.copy:
Gael Monfils had already confirmed that the would retire at the end of the 2026 season, but the star’s career might already be over. Fans began to speculate when the star’s status was changed to ‘retired’ on the International Tennis Integrity Agency’s official website, but many were surprised by the timing.

Monfils was expected to bring his career to a close on home soil, at the Paris Masters, the final Masters tournament on the ATP Tour. The French tournament is due to take place between the 2nd and 8th November, and it would have marked Monfils’ 12th appearance at his home event.

bullets: Emma Raducanu has fallen out of the world's top 100 and now sits 107th, making her British No.3 behind Katie Boulter and Fran Jones. The 23-year-old has not played since losing the Queen's Club final to Donna Vekic in June, and a stress fracture in her right leg has kept her out of Wimbledon and the US Open. She was on the entry list for the China Open but withdrew.

If Raducanu is out for at least six months, she can ask the WTA for a protected ranking of 31st, her position when she was injured. That would let her enter up to eight tournaments, including a maximum of two Grand Slams, next season. Andy Roddick said on his Served podcast in August that she might not be seen for the rest of the year, adding that a stress fracture has to heal to avoid long-term damage.

The situation has seen Raducanu, who missed Wimbledon and the US Open, slide to 107th in the world and become the British No.3 behind Katie Boulter and Fran Jones. As her injury problems continue, the 23-year-old could potentially receive a huge rankings boost by cutting her season short as she makes her way back to full fitness.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: Straight Off the Road, Li Rocks Pusarla
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: Straight Off the Road, Li Rocks Pusarla BWF World Tour
bullets: Germany's Yvonne Li, ranked 45th in the world, beat India's Pusarla V. Sindhu 13-21 25-23 21-19 in 65 minutes in the first round of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 in Odense. Li was promoted from the reserves list into the main draw late on Monday evening and drove three hours from Hamburg on the morning of the match.

Li said she slowed the tempo and found variation from the front court so Sindhu could not attack easily. Sindhu said her disappointment was about her unforced errors rather than the length of the match. Li won the Dutch Open in September and reached the second round of last week's Arctic Open. She credited a change of training environment two years ago, after the Olympics, and said her coach now travels with her more. She next faces India's Tanvi Sharma, who beat Natsuki Nidaira 21-17 16-21 21-19.
Racket.copy:
Yvonne Li’s day began with a message and a decision. Late on Monday evening, she was informed she had been promoted from the reserves list into the main draw of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026. By sunrise, she was in her car, making the three-hour journey from Hamburg to Odense. A few hours later, she was standing on Court 2 having pulled off one of the biggest results of the opening round – the world No.45 stunned Pusarla V. Sindhu 13-21 25-23 21-19 in a 65-minute thriller.

“I got the message last night and drove to Odense this morning,” Li said. “After a three-hour drive, I just played. I can’t really believe it.” After being outplayed in the opening game, Li gradually wrestled control from the Indian shuttler. She found greater variation at the net and slowed the tempo at crucial moments, forcing Pusarla out of her comfort zone.

Racket.title: Will the Six Kings Slam go ahead? Withdrawal of one player could end the richest event in tennis

bullets: This year's Six Kings Slam in Riyadh, due to start on 21 October, is in doubt after militants struck King Khalid International Airport, killing at least 12 people and injuring more than 300. The attacks were claimed by Yemen's Houthi movement, and a NOTAM says the airport remains closed until 21:00 GMT on Saturday, 17 October.

Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien are scheduled to play, each with a $1.5m appearance fee. Governments are advising foreign tourists against travelling to Riyadh, and the Alcaraz, Djokovic and Zverev camps have not commented. Andy Roddick said on his Served podcast that he would not go, as it is an exhibition and the payday would not offset the risk.
Racket.copy:
The countdown is on to the richest event in tennis, but there has to be a huge cloud of uncertainty hanging over this year’s Six Kings Slam. Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien are all scheduled to play in an exhibition event in Saudi Arabia that offers a $1.5 million appearance fee for each competitor.

That money could be collected from playing just one best-of-three-set match in Riyadh, but the challenge for event organisers this year is the current security issue in the host city.

Racket.title: Will Carlos Alcaraz’s ‘protest’ against the ATP Tour turn into a full scale revolt?
Racket.summary: Alcaraz is not happy with extended Masters 1000 tournaments - will he skip playing in 2027? The post Will Carlos Alcaraz’s ‘protest’ against the ATP Tour turn into a full scale revolt? appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz has expressed frustration at the number of mandatory events on the ATP Tour and may follow through on a threat to miss key tournaments in 2027. He won the ATP 500 title in Tokyo days after the Laver Cup in London, and has suggested he would skip parts of next season to avoid a repeat of the wrist injury that followed the Barcelona Open in April and kept him out until mid-August.

Masters 1000 events are mandatory for top players, carry no appearance fees and now run for 12 days. Tim Henman told Tennis365 the format is too much tennis and should be cut to eight or nine days, while Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have made similar claims. Alcaraz is reportedly declining some ATP Tour media team requests as a 'mini protest' and could face financial penalties for skipping events when fit.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz has expressed his frustration at the number of mandatory events on the ATP Tour and he may now follow through with his threat to miss key events in 2027. Alcaraz won the ATP 500 title in Tokyo last week and appeared to enjoy his time on court at an event he opted to play despite the quick turnaround from the Laver Cup in London a few days earlier.

While a player who has already collected over $66 million in career prize money is not likely to be entirely focused on money at this point in his career, Alcaraz would have been paid a big fee for his appearance in Tokyo.

bullets: Seventeen-year-old Amer Mohammed made a statement for Saudi Arabia at the VICTOR BWF World Juniors Championships 2026, beating the Philippines' Ron Ezekiel Zacarias 18-16 15-11 to reach the men's singles Round of 32. He had earlier beaten Thailand's Pannachai Boommak in the second round, and also progressed in mixed doubles with Nabiha Shariff, beating Aiden Dednam/Melay Pretorius 15-6 15-6 to make the Round of 64.

Mohammed next faces second seed and Asian Junior champion Riyan Malhan of the UAE, who beat Korea's Jeong Da Hwan 18-16 15-7 after saving five game points at 9-14, his first win in three meetings. Mohammed won doubles titles at the South Africa Junior International late last year and the Uganda Junior International earlier this year. In men's doubles, Alwathiq Alabidi/Abdulaziz Almuqahwi lost 15-10 15-10 to Thailand's Kunlapat Lhothong/Tachin Wiriyachairerk.
Racket.copy:
Saudi Arabia has been a fleeting presence on the world badminton scene, but 17-year-old Amer Mohammed has made a statement for the country at the VICTOR BWF World Juniors Championships 2026.

Having beaten Pannachai Boommak of Thailand in the second round, Mohammed made his way past Philippines’ Ron Ezekiel Zacarias today, 18-16 15-11, to enter the Round of 32. “It really means a lot, another step in the story,” said Mohammed. “It’s been great, and I’m looking forward to more.

Racket.title: ‘A kind of death’ – ATP veteran opens up on painful reality of being ‘past his prime’
Racket.summary: The Frenchman doesn't want to retire just yet. The post ‘A kind of death’ – ATP veteran opens up on painful reality of being ‘past his prime’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Adrian Mannarino, 38 and ranked 78th, has no plans to retire but admits it is hard to accept that he is "past his prime". The Frenchman beat sixth seed Flavio Cobolli in the second round of the Shanghai Masters. His best year came in 2023, when he finished ranked 22nd with three ATP Tour titles and three top-10 wins.

Speaking to L'Equipe, Mannarino said he knows he will never be as fast or as enduring as before, calling that "a kind of death" for a tennis player. He said he still enjoys the sport and that it pays very well, and he may play another year or two. The five-time tour title winner, who has earned over $15m in prize money, said that cutting training intensity quickly hurts his results.
Racket.copy:
Adrian Mannarino has no plans to retire just yet, but the veteran admits it is hard to accept that he is “past his prime”. The 38-year-old currently sits at 78th in the world and is more than capable of pulling off an upset, something he did in his second-round win over sixth seed Flavio Cobolli at the Shanghai Masters.

The Frenchman had the best year of his career at the age of 35 when he finished 2023 with a year-end ranking of 22, which included three ATP Tour titles and three top 10 victories.

Racket.title: Jannik Sinner urged to follow Rafael Nadal’s example amid growing injury concerns
Racket.summary: Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have opted for a similar strategy. The post Jannik Sinner urged to follow Rafael Nadal’s example amid growing injury concerns appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Tennis analyst Gill Gross has urged Jannik Sinner to be more transparent about the knee injury that has ended his season, saying in an Instagram video that he sees little downside to doing so. Sinner, 25, beat Alexander Zverev in four sets to defend his Wimbledon title in mid-July and is not expected to play again until 2027.

Gross contrasted Sinner with Rafael Nadal, who regularly gave fans detailed injury updates, and said openness would help stop speculation. Little has been disclosed about Carlos Alcaraz's wrist injury either. Separately, Rick Macci, Serena Williams' former coach, dismissed talk that Sinner is serving a "silent" doping ban. Such talk likely stems from his three-month ban in 2025 after twice testing positive for clostebol in March 2024. Sinner's entourage appears content with its current strategy.
Racket.copy:
Jannik Sinner has been urged to be more “transparent” about the knee injury that prematurely ended his season. When Sinner defended his Wimbledon title after beating Alexander Zverev in four sets in mid-July, very few would have predicted he wouldn’t play again until 2027.

The 25-year-old has struggled with his injury under wraps. While Rafael Nadal used to provide regular updates on his injuries over the years, tennis fans have not been told a great deal about Alcaraz’s wrist injury and Sinner’s current issue.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev issues telling injury update after Shanghai Masters scare
Racket.summary: "I'm starting to feel my body more and more." The post Alexander Zverev issues telling injury update after Shanghai Masters scare appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev beat world No 22 Alexander Bublik 7-6(6), 4-6, 7-6(1) in the Shanghai Masters last 16 on Tuesday, despite appearing to be in discomfort. The world No 2 saved four set points and recovered from 3-6 down in the first-set tiebreak. After losing serve in the opening game of the decider, he broke straight back to love.

The 29-year-old had an ankle problem during earlier wins over Wu Yibing and Quentin Halys. He told Tennis TV it was "acting up, unfortunately, again", which he called understandable given how much he has played. He described becoming world No 1 for the first time later this year as special, bringing a sense of responsibility, particularly as he is close to 30. He meets world No 9 Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev provided an injury update after he appeared to be in discomfort during his fourth round win at the 2026 Shanghai Masters. The two-time Grand Slam champion prevailed 7-6(6), 4-6, 7-6(1) against world No 22 Alexander Bublik in a pulsating last 16 clash in Shanghai on Tuesday.

World No 2 Zverev fought off four set points and recovered from a 3-6 deficit in the tiebreak to sneak through the first set. After Bublik earned the only break of the second set en route to levelling the match, Zverev found himself in trouble when he lost serve again in the opening game of the final set.

Racket.title: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open
Racket.summary: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open Sky Sports
bullets: Alexander Zverev beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) to reach the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals, in his first match since clinching the year-end world No 1 ranking for the first time on Monday. The French Open and US Open champion admitted his ankle was "acting up". He next plays ninth seed Alex de Minaur, who beat Karen Khachanov 6-3 6-4.

Current world No 1 Jannik Sinner is out for the rest of 2026 with a knee injury, and Carlos Alcaraz cannot overtake Zverev this year. Zverev said finishing as world No 1 brings a different responsibility. Elsewhere, Katie Boulter lost 6-3 6-1 to 11th seed Diana Shnaider in the Wuhan Open first round. Iga Swiatek is 10th in the qualifying table for the WTA Finals (8-15 November, Indian Wells), with four of the eight spots still available.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters. Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win.

The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance.

Racket.title: Rafael Nadal hits back at claims he’s heard about Carlos Alcaraz recently – ‘Makes no sense’
Racket.summary: Nadal is against what people are saying about Carlos Alcaraz. The post Rafael Nadal hits back at claims he’s heard about Carlos Alcaraz recently – ‘Makes no sense’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Rafael Nadal has rejected the description of Carlos Alcaraz as a "prospect", following Alcaraz's exit from the Shanghai Masters. As reported by Kalshi Tennis, Nadal said that with seven Grand Slams Alcaraz is not just a promise for the future but already a legend, noting few players in history have won seven. Nadal partnered Alcaraz in doubles at the Paris Olympics.

Alcaraz, 23, has more Grand Slam titles than Stefan Edberg and Boris Becker, and the same number as Mats Wilander and John McEnroe. He became the youngest player to complete the Career Grand Slam earlier this year by winning the Australian Open for the first time, and has finished as year-end world No 1 twice. He has yet to win the Paris Masters or the ATP Finals.
Racket.copy:
In many ways, Carlos Alcaraz took the torch from Rafael Nadal when he retired from the sport in 2024. Nadal dominated the Spanish tennis landscape for nearly two decades before Alcaraz arrived as a fresh-faced tennis towards the end of the 2010s.

As Nadal’s playing career was coming to an end, Alcaraz began to make a name for himself on the ATP Tour. He was a four-time Grand Slam winner by the time the Spaniard called time on his playing career.

Racket.title: Italian media reveal Jannik Sinner’s injury treatment plan under supervision of renowned specialist
Racket.summary: "We are sure that even Jannik, number one in the world, in the coming months will recover well." The post Italian media reveal Jannik Sinner’s injury treatment plan under supervision of renowned specialist appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Jannik Sinner has started treatment on his injured knee, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The world No 1 has been absent from the ATP Tour since Wimbledon and announced last week that his 2026 season was over, so he will not return before 2027. He has already received platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment from Lyon-based orthopaedic surgeon Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet, who has operated on several Juventus players and examined Kylian Mbappe's knee.

Rehabilitation will be run through the Physioclinic centre under its co-founder Dr Herbert Schoenhuber, who helped Italian skier Sofia Goggia recover for the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, where she won silver. The connection comes through the friendship between Sinner's agent, Alex Vittur, and skier Alberto Tomba, whom Schoenhuber has also treated. Most physiotherapy and training will take place in Monte Carlo, with a return in Australia early in 2027 if all goes to plan.
Racket.copy:
Jannik Sinner has started treatment on his injured knee with Italian media confirming he will be treated by a renowned sports medicine specialist. The reigning world No 1 has been absent from the ATP Tour since Wimbledon due to a knee injury and he won’t return to action before 2027 as he announced last week that the “2026 season is officially over” as reveal “I need to think about my long-term career”.

Sinner and his team have given very little away about the full extent of his injury, but more information has now emerged about the rehabilitation plan for the coming months. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the five-time Grand Slam winner has already received Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) treatment by Lyon-based orthopaedic surgeon Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet – who has operated on several Juventus players in recent months while he also examined French and Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe’s injured knee.

Racket.title: ‘Alex Eala will be fine – but she needs to make a big change after shock Wuhan Open loss’
Racket.summary: A legendary coach has shared his thoughts after Alex Eala's defeat in Wuhan. The post ‘Alex Eala will be fine – but she needs to make a big change after shock Wuhan Open loss’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alex Eala, the world No 19 and 13th seed, lost 4-6, 6-3, 6-3 to 217th-ranked qualifier Shi Han in the opening round of the WTA 1000 Wuhan Open on Monday. The 21-year-old led 6-4, 3-2 but lost the next seven games and fell 0-3 down in the decider. It was her first match since losing to Wang Xiyu in the Asian Games semi-finals.

Coach Rick Macci, a former coach of Serena and Venus Williams, said on X that Eala "will be fine" and has many of the boxes checked for a top-ten player, but that her serve needs "reconstructive surgery". He described her movement as the X factor, saying that if her ball speed or on-the-rise striking diminishes she will be in a "Filipino street fight". Eala sits one place below her career-high ranking of 18th, first reached in August.
Racket.copy:
A legendary coach has assessed that Alex Eala “will be fine” after her shock loss at the 2026 Wuhan Open while also arguing that her serve needs “reconstructive surgery.” World No 19 Eala was stunned 4-6, 6-3, 6-3 by 217th-ranked qualifier Shi Han in the opening round at the WTA 1000 event in Wuhan on Monday.

The 21-year-old, who was seeded 13th in Wuhan, was playing her first match since her defeat to Wang Xiyu in the semi-finals of the Asian Games. Eala led 6-4, 3-2 against Shi, but she lost the next seven games to find herself 0-3 down in the decider before her 21-year-old Chinese opponent sealed the win in convincing fashion.

Racket.title: Carlos Alcaraz said to be protesting ‘behind the scenes’ at the Shanghai Masters
Racket.summary: Alcaraz is not happy. The post Carlos Alcaraz said to be protesting ‘behind the scenes’ at the Shanghai Masters appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz criticised the ATP Tour schedule at the Shanghai Masters, saying officials are pushing players too far by asking them to play so many tournaments and matches, which he cited as one reason for injuries. The world No 3 said it is "getting in the wrong direction" and wished Jannik Sinner well after Sinner ended his season early.

Catherine Whittaker of The Tennis Podcast said she believes Alcaraz is staging low-key protests behind the scenes, including abstaining from ATP marketing. She said 500-level events suit him, with decent fields and appearance fees, whereas Masters 1000s feel like a grind. Alcaraz lost in the third round in Miami and Shanghai and in the Indian Wells semi-finals to Daniil Medvedev, and reached the Monte Carlo final, losing to Sinner. A wrist injury in April cost him Madrid, the Italian Open, Canada and Cincinnati.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz has issued his disatisfaction with the ATP Tour schedule while at the Shanghai Masters. Jannik Sinner deciding to end his season early appeared to be the final straw for the Spaniard, and he produced a scathing attack on the authorities while at the Masters event.

“One of the reasons we had to see the players who are getting injured, they [ATP officials] are pushing us too much out of the line sometimes to play a lot of tournaments, to play a lot of matches.

Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz suffered another early exit at the Shanghai Masters as he was beaten in straight sets by Zizou Bergs in the third round. Alcaraz has played the Chinese Masters tournament three times in his career now, and his best effort is a sole quarterfinal appearance in 2024.

Racket.title: Boulter beaten by Shnaider in Wuhan

Boulter said in a social media tribute that she had experienced "a tough week".

Racket.title: Why Emma Raducanu shouldn't return for three months after hitting two-year low
Racket.summary: Why Emma Raducanu shouldn't return for three months after hitting two-year low The Sun
bullets: Emma Raducanu, 23, has fallen to 107th in the world rankings, her lowest position since August 2024. She has not played since suffering a stress fracture in her right foot after a straight-sets loss to Donna Vekic in the Queen's final on 14 June, when she was ranked 31st the next day. She pulled out of Wimbledon and the US Open, and is now British No 3 behind Katie Boulter (54) and Fran Jones (104).

Raducanu is not on the entry list for the final six tournaments of 2026. If she stays out until January, she can petition for a protected ranking, available after six months out through physical injury. The ranking would be frozen at the point of injury and allow up to eight events, including a maximum of two Grand Slams. It would put her in the 2027 Australian Open main draw, but unseeded. Her team is giving no update on her recovery.
Racket.copy:
EMMA RADUCANU will be eligible for special fitness status – provided she resists the urge to return to competition this year. The former US Open champion, 23, has not played since suffering a stress fracture in her right foot on Sunday, June 14 following a straight-sets loss to Croatian Donna Vekic in the WTA Queen’s final.

Raducanu – who was spotted hobbling around London in an orthopaedic moon boot – pulled out of Wimbledon and then the US Open and has been absent for the past four months. She also has a long-standing issue with her right ankle and lower shin.

Racket.title: Alex de Minaur provides injury update after reaching the Shanghai Masters quarterfinal

bullets: Alex de Minaur has reached the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals, beating Rei Sakamoto and Karen Khachanov, about a week after retiring from his China Open final against Novak Djokovic with a groin injury. He said the groin has felt better every day over the seven to eight days since, with a focus on recovery, and that his latest match was "very clean".

He next faces Alexander Zverev, who has beaten him eight times on the ATP Tour, including in Shanghai, Indian Wells and the Italian Open. De Minaur has won their last two meetings, both Laver Cup matches in London and San Francisco, as well as at the United Cup and ATP Cup. Only Felix Auger-Aliassime and Daniil Medvedev remain in the draw ranked higher than him. A good run could help confirm his ATP Finals place.
Racket.copy:
Alex de Minaur’s season looked to be derailed when he was forced out of his China Open final against Novak Djokovic. The player retired from the match due to a groin injury against the Serbian star, with many fearing the worse for the rest of the star’s season.

However, the Australian has bounced back at the Shanghai Masters by reaching the last eight of the penultimate Masters event on the ATP Tour. De Minaur has beaten Rei Sakamoto and Karen Khachanov to reach the quarterfinals of the competition, where he will await the winner of Alexander Zverev or Alexander Bublik.

Racket.title: Zizou Bergs offers blunt response to Carlos Alcaraz’s ball complaints
Racket.summary: "It's not an issue with the balls," says Bergs. The post Zizou Bergs offers blunt response to Carlos Alcaraz’s ball complaints appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Zizou Bergs, the world No 39, beat Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6 (7-4) in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Monday, the biggest win of his career. Alcaraz, the world No 3 and reigning Australian Open champion, was overheard telling his team "I can't play like this". He said afterwards that the ball was bigger and slower and the court felt different from his opening match.

Bergs said the balls were the same as at the Japan Open, which Alcaraz won on his return from a four-month wrist-injury layoff. He said the balls and court are "in general very good", though an occasional bad bounce can happen. Bergs added that he has often had too much respect for big names and was too much in the moment to celebrate, which is why he wrote "what just happened" on the camera.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz was quite vocal about his unhappiness with the balls being used at the Shanghai Masters, but the man who beat him in the third round says the “balls are in general very good”.

Seven-time Grand Slam winner Alcaraz suffered a shock defeat to Zizou Bergs on Monday as the Belgian claimed the biggest win of his career, beating the reigning Australian Open champion 7-5, 7-6 (7-4).

Carlos Alcaraz suffered one of his earliest defeats of the season as he was dispatched in the third round of the Shanghai Masters at the hands of Zizou Bergs. Alcaraz had entered the Shanghai Masters in impressive form, having won the Japan Open title at his previous tournament.

The Spaniard looked set to continue that form when he comprehensively defeated Juan Manuel Cerundolo to set up a third round meeting with Bergs. Golf.title: Rules Guy: My ball won't stop rolling when I place it. What now?
Golf.summary: What do you do if your ball won't stop rolling when you place it? How should you proceed? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: My ball won’t stop rolling when I place it. What now? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: In this Rules Guy column, a reader asks about a ball resting on the lip of a bunker, held in place by a rake handle. When the rake is moved and the ball replaced, it rolls closer to the hole into a better lie in the fairway. The answer is that the player cannot play from the new position. The rake is a movable obstruction, and under Rule 15.2 the ball must be put back.

If the ball will not stay put after a second attempt, Rule 14.2e says the player must find the nearest spot in the correct area, not nearer the hole, where it will stay. A second reader asks about a ball on a green that was blown off by a gust of wind during a ruling delay for a playing partner. Under Rule 9.3, a ball moved by natural forces is played as it lies, unless it had already been lifted and replaced.
Golf.copy:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. My approach shot landed on the lip of the bunker, held in place by the handle of the sand rake. If I move the handle, the ball drops into the sand trap. The rules state the rake is a movable object and can be moved with the ball replaced to its original spot. Here’s the rub: the ball won’t stay put — it rolls down the shoulder of the bunker closer to the hole, and in a more favorable lie in the fairway. Can I play from the new position? —Richard Fetterman, Banning, CA

Nice and reasonable though that may sound, Richard, verily you cannot. Though it was held in place by the rake, your ball came to rest on a specific spot. That rake, as you note, is a movable obstruction, but per Rule 15.2 you need to put the ball back if it then moves.

The fix started earlier in the swing, with the clubface on the takeaway and then his trail arm, which he over-bent on the backswing, flattening the top of his swing and creating a steep transition.

To build structure in the trail arm, Travis used the AMG Arm Shark, a strap with a magnetic fin that releases with a noise when the arm moves outside the correct range. Golf.copy:

Golf.copy:
'Inside The Ropes' is the chance for Golf Monthly's expert team to share its honest thoughts on the biggest subjects in the game. This time, it's all about the futures of Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and LIV Golf'.

It's set to be a critical next few weeks for LIV Golf and its hopes of a '2.0' version coming to fruition, with its bankruptcy case rolling on and players deciding whether to commit or go elsewhere.

Golf.title: Can A 3-Handicap Golfer Break Par If Rory McIlroy Hits The Tee Shots?

Golf.copy:

Then there's the next chasm in technique from elite level amateur to PGA Tour player, making my golfing ability feel especially ordinary relatively speaking.

Driving has always been one of my weaker areas too. But what if I could swap out my shambolic tee shots and sub in one of the best drivers of our generation? How would my short game hold up and could I shoot under par around a ‘normal’ parkland course?

bullets: Cole Hammer, 27, missed out on a PGA Tour card at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship after a final-round 73 left him tied 43rd. He began the week 20th in the season-long standings, the last position that earns a card, but five Sunday bogeys, including one on his second-to-last hole, dropped him to 22nd. David Lamb, who started the week 23rd, finished 20th to take the final card.

Hammer, who helped Texas win the 2022 NCAA title and was named the world's best amateur in 2019, said ball striking let him down and that he was "dejected". He added that he still believes in himself and described his pursuit of a card as "a fun journey" of five or six years of learning. He will play another season on the Korn Ferry Tour.
Golf.copy:
Sunday saw a host of young and journeyman pros alike experience the highlight of their careers: earning PGA Tour cards at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship. As happens every year, heartwarming tales about players’ big achievements abound. But there is another side to the story: the other pros who just missed out on their Tour cards.

On Sunday, the pain that group felt was best exemplified by Cole Hammer. The 27-year-old Texas pro narrowly lost his grasp on his own Tour card with a poor final round on Sunday. But instead of fleeing the course as fast as he could, a “dejected” Hammer faced the cameras and opened up about his unfortunate fate. In the process, he showed a hard-earned perspective that should serve him well as he continues his pro career.

The stance follows the Saudi PIF's April announcement that it would withdraw financial support for LIV, and eight conditional releases granted in February.

Roughly 15 players with status on both tours are likely to be affected, including Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin. Jon Rahm has ruled himself out of the new LIV league, so he looks set to return to the DP World Tour full-time in 2027. Joaquin Niemann and Thomas Pieters would have to enter Q-School or agree a deal for guaranteed invites, and a player who says they will not play LIV but then does so could have their membership cancelled immediately.
Golf.copy:

First reported by BBC Sport, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings is on record as saying "players must make a choice" in terms of where they will play next season and beyond. Golf.copy:
If you haven’t heard, big changes are coming to the PGA Tour in 2028. With the Tour’s two-track system debuting in a little over a year, that means next season, 2027, will be critical for players trying to play their way onto the top tier, the Championship Series.

And you know what’s really going to help accomplish that? By already owning a PGA Tour card in 2027. Twenty players just did that — including a 19-year-old pro — as they earned a promotion via the season-ending Korn Ferry Tour Championship Sunday. Now those guys have a head start in getting on the top track come 2028.

Alongside his 18 Korn Ferry starts in 2026, he made 11 PGA Tour starts, making nine cuts and finishing in the top 20 seven times. Golf.copy:
Sunday may not have been the exact result 19-year-old Blades Brown was looking for — a fourth 54-hole lead squandered — but it ultimately saw him earn what he wanted next: a season full of starts on the PGA Tour.

Brown is well known to this point, partly due to his golfy name and partly due to his impressive game. He turned pro at just 17 and has played on the Korn Ferry Tour much of the last two seasons, occasionally sprinkling in some starts on the PGA Tour. He flashed in moments this summer, never quite getting across the line for a win, but the floor has been extremely high. He’s made 16 of 18 cuts and finished in the top 10 five times.

bullets: David Lipsky's caddie, Darren Woolard, reportedly told him to find someone else to carry his bag before the final round of the Baycurrent Classic in Japan, according to Golfweek. Lipsky, 38, finished in a share of 54th at Yokohama Country Club on three under and shot a one-under 70 on Sunday. It is unclear who caddied for him, though some claim it was his trainer.
