The split came a month after Alejandro Tosti's caddie, Cliff Ellis, walked off midway through the first round of the Biltmore Championship in September. Lipsky has made 160 PGA Tour starts and earned $8 million in prize money.
Golf.copy:
Players splitting with caddies is nothing new in the professional game but, in the last month, we have seen two players split with their loopers mid-event. The first came back at the Biltmore Championship in September, when Alejandro Tosti's caddie, Cliff Ellis, walked off midway through the first round, with the other occurring at this week's Baycurrent Classic.

Taking place in Japan, the 72-man tournament was won by Michael Brennan, who secured a one stroke win over Keith Mitchell and Jacob Bridgeman. Less than 12 hours on from the win, though, news broke that one player in the tournament had split with his caddie prior to a ball being struck on the final round on Sunday.

Golf.title: Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win
Golf.summary: Scotland's Grant Forrest holds off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year.
bullets: Scotland's Grant Forrest held off home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open, earning a place at The Open and the Masters next year. Chacarra was in the clubhouse on 13 under, so Forrest and Victor Perez needed birdies at the 18th. After Perez's putt drifted past, Forrest holed his to claim a third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Forrest began the final round sharing the lead with England's Joe Dean on 13 under. He made bogeys at the third, sixth and eighth but recovered with three birdies and a bogey in five holes at the start of the back nine. A closing one-under 70 earned the £480,000 first prize. Forrest said he was in pure shock after a tough year and could not believe he was going to Augusta.
Golf.copy:
Scotland's Grant Forrest held off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year. With Chacarra in the clubhouse at 13 under, Forrest and playing partner Victor Perez needed to make birdies at the 18th to go above the Spaniard.

Both players' drives nestled down in the greenside rough on the 322-yard par four, and after Perez's birdie putt drifted past the hole, Forrest sunk his to seal his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Golf.title: How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson
Golf.summary: Alistair Docherty joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to discuss finally earning his PGA Tour card, his first golf memory and more. The post How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Alistair Docherty, 32, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time in 2027, told this week's GOLF Subpar podcast that his first golf memory was the 2010 U.S. Senior Open at Sahalee Country Club in Sammamish, Washington. He attended with his father and they sat by the 10th tee.

Bernhard Langer hit his tee shot into one of the course's many evergreens there. Docherty said he told his father that pros hit bad shots too. Langer went on to win that week, which taught Docherty that one bad shot does not determine the outcome. Sahalee also hosted the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.
Golf.copy:
Alistair Docherty’s first golf memory provided a couple of valuable lessons. The 32-year-old pro, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time come 2027, joined this week’s GOLF Subpar podcast and explained how a trip to Sahalee Country Club played a key role in his life.

Sahalee is a private country club in Sammamish, Wash., just outside of Seattle, and in 2010 it hosted the U.S. Senior Open. (It was also home to the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.) But in 2010, Docherty attended the U.S. Senior Open with his father, and they found a spot to sit by the 10th tee.

Golf.title: 'Fairytale stuff': Pro's hard year ends with ticket to 2027 Masters
Golf.summary: Grant Forrest has had a year to forget. But that all changed on Sunday in Spain, where he punched an unlikely ticket to the 2027 Masters. The post ‘Fairytale stuff’: Pro’s hard year ends with ticket to 2027 Masters appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Grant Forrest won the Open de España presented by Madrid, finishing 14 under to earn places in the 2027 Masters and the Open Championship at St Andrews. He had opened with rounds of 66-66-67 to share the 54-hole lead with Joe Dean. After going out in 2-over 38 on Sunday, he birdied the 13th and 14th, then holed a winning birdie putt at the driveable par-four 18th after chipping to five feet.

Forrest lost the 2015 Amateur Championship final 4&2 to Romain Langasque, which cost him a Masters place. His earlier DP World Tour wins came at the 2021 Hero Open and the 2025 Nexo Championship. He arrived in Madrid with one top-10 and three top-20s in 2026, and had not finished better than 63rd since June. He described the win as fairytale stuff.
Golf.copy:
Eleven years ago, Grant Forrest had a ticket to the Masters in his grasp. Then a budding Scottish amateur star, Forrest reached the finals of the 2015 Amateur Championship. A win meant not only one of amateur golf’s biggest prizes but also a trip to Magnolia Lane. But a 4&2 loss to Romain Langasque meant Forrest’s Augusta National dream would have to wait.

The wait wasn’t expected to be long. Forrest made the 2015 Walker Cup team and was expected to be one of Europe’s bright young stars. But golf had other plans. Forrest turned pro and worked his way up from the Challenge Tour to the DP World Tour, finally reaching the top European circuit in 2019. His first DP World Tour win arrived at the 2021 Hero Open. His next came four years later at the 2025 Nexo Championship. Along the way, Forrest played in two Open Championships and one U.S. Open, but never played well enough to reach Augusta National.

bullets: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic at Yokohama Country Club, holding off Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell for his third PGA Tour title in 12 months. Golf.copy:
Sunday at Yokohama Country Club began with a packed leaderboard and a world of possibilities. It ended with Michael Brennan holding off Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell to win the Baycurrent Classic, his third PGA Tour title in 12 months.

“Unbelievable. It was an unbelievable week. Japan was spectacular, the fans were amazing this week,” Brennan said after his win. Mitchell, who is still searching for his first win since the 2019 Honda Classic, took the lead on the front nine with three birdies and an eagle. But he dropped shots at Nos. 9 and 12, leaving him one shot behind Brennan coming down the stretch. Mitchell striped his tee shot on 18 and left himself a 10-foot birdie putt to tie Brennan at 16 under, but he couldn’t get it to fall.
